UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1939 ANSWERED ON 30 TH JULY, 2026 
ASKED BY SHRI SHYAMKUMAR DAULAT BARVE REGARDING ROAD 
ACCIDENTS, FATALITIES AND ROAD SAFETY. 
  
Details of various initiatives taken by the Government in Ministry of 
Road Transport and Highways for road safety: - 
  
(1)  Education:  
i.  Administers a scheme for setting up of Institutes of Driving 
Training & Research (IDTRs), Regional Driving Training Centres 
(RDTCs) and Driving Training Centres (DTCs) at State/district level 
across the Country.  Recently revised scheme guidelines have been 
issued, incorporating enhanced financial assistance and 
streamlined eligibility criteria for establishing Driving Training 
Institutes. Additionally, incentives have been introduced for setting 
up Automated Testing Stations (ATS) in conjunction with Driving 
Training Institutes (DTIs) under the Training -Testing Cluster 
approach. 
ii.  Administers Road Safety Advo cacy Scheme for raising 
awareness about road safety and for administering road safety 
programs. 
iii.  Observance of National Road Safety Month every year for 
spreading awareness and strengthening road safety.      
  
(2)       Engineering: 
  
2.1.    Road engineering: 
i.  Road Safety Audit (RSA) of all National Highways (NHs) has 
been made mandatory through third party auditors/ experts at all 
stages i.e. design, construction, operation and maintenance etc.  
ii.  High priority is accorded to identification an d rectification of 
black spots /accident spots on NHs. 
iii.  Road Safety Officer (RSO) has been designated at each 
Regional Office of road owning agencies   to look after RSA and 
other road safety related works. 
iv.  Administers the electronic Detailed Acci dent Report (e -DAR) 
Project to establish a central repository for reporting, management 
and analysis of road accidents data across the Country. 

v.  Issued guidelines for the provision of signages on 
Expressways and National Highways to offer improved visib ility and 
intuitive guidance to the drivers.  
vi.  Provisions have been made in the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 
for failure to comply with standards for the road design, 
construction and maintenance, as prescribed by the Central 
Government from time to time.  
  
2.2    Vehicle engineering: Various initiatives were undertaken to 
make vehicles safer, including the following:-  
i.  Mandatory provision of an airbag for the passenger seated on 
the front seat of a vehicle, next to the driver. 
ii.  Prescribed norms re lated to safety measures for children 
below four years of age, riding or being carried on a motor cycle. It 
also specifies use of a safety harness, crash helmet and restricts 
speed to 40kmph. 
iii.  Mandatory provisions for fitment of following listed safet y 
technologies: - 
For M1 category vehicles: 
a. Seat Belt Reminder (SBR) for driver and co-driver. 
b. Manual Override for central locking system 
c. Over speed warning system. 
For all M and N category vehicles: 
a. Reverse Parking Alert System 
iv.  Mandated Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) for certain classes 
of L [Motor vehicle with less than four wheels and includes a 
Quadricycle], M [Motor vehicles with at least four wheels used for 
carrying passengers] and N [Motor vehicles with at least four 
wheels used for carrying goods which may also carry persons in 
addition to goods, subject to conditions stipulated in BIS standards] 
categories.  
v.  Mandated speed limiting function/speed limiting device in all 
transport vehicles, except for two wheelers, thre e wheelers, 
quadricycles, fire tenders, ambulances and police vehicles. 
vi.  Published the rules for recognition, regulation and control of 
Automated Testing Stations, which define the procedure for fitness 
testing of vehicles through automated equipment a nd the procedure 
for grant of fitness certificate by ATSs. The rules have been further 
amended on 31.10.2022 and 14.03.2024. 
vii.  Formulated the Vehicle Scrapping Policy based on 
incentives/dis-incentives and for creating an ecosystem to phase 
out old, unfit and polluting vehicles. 

viii.  Formulated a Scheme to set up one model Inspection & 
Certification Centre in each State/UT with Central assistance for 
testing the fitness of vehicles through an automated system. 
ix.  Published rules regarding the Bharat  New Car Assessment 
Program (BNCAP) to introduce the concept of safety rating of 
passenger cars and empower consumers to take informed 
decisions. 
x.  Published rules regarding prescribed level playing field in the 
area of manufacturing of buses by Original  Equipment 
Manufacturers (OEMs) and Bus Body Builders.   
xi.  Mandated vehicles, manufactured on or after 1st October, 
2025, shall be fitted with an air -conditioning system for the cabin of 
vehicles of N2 (goods vehicle with gross vehicle weight exceeding 
3.5 tonnes but not exceeding 12.0 tonnes) and N3 (goods vehicle 
with gross vehicle weight exceeding 12.0 tonnes) category. 
xii.  Published rules for revision of standards for Safety Belt, 
Restraint Systems and Safety Belt Reminder to provide provisions 
for applicability of revised standards for safety belt assemblies, 
safety belt anchorages and the installation of Safety Belts and 
Restraint Systems, in Motor vehicles of category M,N and L7 w.e.f. 
01st April, 2025. Further, the vehicles of category M1, manuf actured 
on and after the 1st April 2025, shall meet the requirement of safety 
belt reminder for all front facing rear seats as per AIS-145-2018. 
xiii.  Published rules for Active safety features in Medium and 
Heavy Duty vehicles, which provide for Braking System including 
Anti-lock Braking, Endurance Braking System for M2, M3, N1, N2, N3 
and Quadricycle (effective for new models from 1st January, 2027 
and for existing models from 1st October, 2027), and Advanced 
Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) including Ve hicle Stability 
Function (VSF), Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS), Driver 
Drowsiness and Attention Warning Systems, Blind Spot Information 
Systems and Moving off Information Systems for M2, M3, N2 and N3 
categories of vehicles (effective for new models from 1st October, 
2027 and for existing models from 1st January, 2028). 
xiv.  Published rule for Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System (AVAS) 
meeting AIS -173 audibility standards has been mandated for 
electric vehicles. The requirement applies to new vehicle mo dels 
manufactured on or after 1st October 2026 and existing vehicle 
models manufactured on or after 1st October 2027. Since electric 
vehicles operate almost silently at low speeds, AVAS generates an 
audible warning sound to alert pedestrians, cyclists, and  especially 
visually impaired persons of an approaching vehicle, thereby 
enhancing road safety. 

  
(3)  Enforcement: 
i.  The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 as stands 
implemented provides for strict penalties for ensuring compliance 
and enhancing deter rence for violation of traffic rules and strict 
enforcement through use of technology. Traffic management  and 
enforcement is essentially in the domain of State Governments/UT 
Administrations. While Central Government formulates rules under 
the Motor Vehicl e Act, 1988, the enforcement of these rules comes 
under the purview of State Governments/UT Administrations.  
ii.  Issued rules for Electronic Monitoring and Enforcement of 
Road Safety. The rules specify the detailed provisions for placement 
of electronic enforcement devices on high risk & high density 
corridors on National Highways, State Highways and critical 
junctions cities having a population of more than one million in the 
country and cities under National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).  
iii.  The Central Government, vide Notification dated 20.01.2026, 
has amended Rules 167 and 167A of the Central Motor Vehicles 
Rules, 1989 to establish a transparent, technology -driven and time -
bound e-Challan framework for issuance, payment and redressal of 
traffic challans. The amendments also provide for online challenge 
of challans, automated notifications and stronger enforcement  
measures to improve compliance and road safety. 
iv.  Government has notified the National Road Safety Board 
Rules, 2025 and in accordance with the provisions of the said Rules, 
the National Road Safety Board has been constituted and notified 
vide S.O. 3505(E) dated 29.06.2026. 
v.  The Central Government has formulated the Guidelines on 
Constitution and Utilization of the State Road Safety Fund (SRSF) 
and Funding to District Road Safety Committees (DRSCs) 2025 to 
ensure sustained financing and accountable i mplementation of road 
safety measures through the establishment of a non -lapsable State 
Road Safety Fund and by empowering District Road Safety 
Committees to undertake targeted road safety interventions at the 
grassroots level. 
vi.  On 10th June, 2024, the Government has issued an advisory to 
all the States and Union territories on technological interventions 
for ensuring compliance with Motor Vehicle Act, 1988. 
vii.  The Government has issued guidelines under the „Programme 
for Accelerated Renewal and Ince ntivization of Vehicle Assets for 
Reducing Transport Air Pollution and Network Emissions 
(PARIVARTAN Scheme)‟ on 14.07.2026 to accelerate the 
replacement of old, polluting vehicles with cleaner and safer 

alternatives. The scheme promotes vehicle scrapping and adoption 
of environmentally friendly vehicles, contributing to improved road 
safety, reduced emissions, and sustainable mobility. 
  
(4)  Emergency care: 
i.  Revised the scheme guidelines (named as Rah -Veer) for the 
protection of Good Samaritan, who in good faith, voluntarily and 
without expectation of any reward or compensation renders 
emergency medical or non -medical care or assistance at the scene 
of an acci dent to the victim or transports such victim to the 
hospital. As per the scheme, the reward for Rah -Veer has been 
increased to Rs. 25,000/- from Rs. 5,000/-. 
ii.  Enhanced compensation of victims of Hit and Run motor 
accidents (from Rs. 12,500 to Rs. 50,00 0 for grievous hurt and from 
Rs. 25,000 to Rs.2,00,000 for death). 
iii.  The National Highways Authority of India has made provisions 
for ambulances with paramedical staff/Emergency Medical 
Technician/Nurse at toll plazas on the completed corridors of 
National Highways. 
iv.  Government has notified the „Prime Minister – Road Accident 
Victims‟ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment (PM-Rahat) Scheme‟ 
(Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025) on 
5th May 2025. Subsequently, detailed operational  guidelines, 
including the process flow, stakeholder -wise Standard Operating 
Procedures (SOPs), and clearly defined roles and responsibilities, 
were notified on 4th June 2025 to facilitate its effective 
implementation.

MINISTRY OF POWER

AUGMENTATION OF POWER GENERATION CAPACITY IN TAMIL NADU 
 
1940. DR. RANI SRIKUMAR:  
SHRI C N ANNADURAI:  
SHRI SELVAM G: 
 
 Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has prepared a long-term plan to augment power 
generation capacity in Tamil Nadu to meet the State's projected electricity 
demand up to the year 2034-35 and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) the details of thermal power generation projects under  construction or 
approved in Tamil Nadu including their proposed capacity, estimated cost and 
expected year of commissioning;  
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the requirement of additional 
thermal power capacity for Tamil Nadu and if so, the details thereof along with 
the steps taken to facilitate timely implementation of the proposed projects;  
 
(d) the measures being taken to ensure adequate coal supply, transmission 
infrastructure and environmental compliance for these projects; and  
 
(e) the expected impa ct of the proposed capacity addition on power 
availability, industrial  growth, agricultural supply and long -term energy 
security in Tamil Nadu? 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER  
 
(SHRI SHRIPAD NAIK)  
 
(a) : Ministry of Power had  notified the Electricity (Amendment) Rules in 
December, 2022. Under Rule 16 of the Electricity (Amendment) Rules, Ministry 
of Power has notified ‘Resource Adequacy (RA)  Guidelines’ in June, 2023.  
 
With a view to ensure generation capacity remains ahead of projected 
peak demand, all the Discoms / States including Tamil Nadu, in consultation 
with Central Electricity Authority (CEA), have prepared their “Resource 
Adequacy Plans (RAPs)” till 2035-36, which are dynamic ten-year rolling plans 
and includes powe r generation as well as power procurement planning, in 
accordance with the above-mentioned guidelines. 
………2. 

 
- 2 - 
 
(b) : The details of the under -construction and proposed thermal power 
projects in the State of Tamil Nadu are given at Annexure-I and Annexure-II 
respectively. 
 
(c) : As per the Resource Adequacy Plan (RAP) of Tamil Nadu till 2035 -36, 
about 12,400 MW additional thermal capacity is required by 2034-35. Of these,  
2,640 MW thermal capacity is under-construction in the State, 1000 MW thermal 
capacity is under bidding, and further, for setting up 660 MW thermal capacity, 
Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) has been issued. Tamil Nadu may either set up the 
balance capacity or tie up power from generation projects located within or 
outside the state. 
 
Ministry of Power through Central Electricity Authority (CEA) monitors 
the progress of under-construction power projects through frequent site visits 
and interaction with the developers and other stakeholders for resolving issues 
critical for projects commissioning. 
 
(d) :  The following steps are being taken to ensure uninterrupted coal supply 
to power plants: 
 
i. To address the issues of coal supplies to power sector, an Inter - 
Ministerial Sub Group comprising of representatives from Ministries of 
Power, Coal, Railways, Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Coal India 
Limited (CIL) and Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) meet 
regularly to take various operational decisions to enhance supply of coal 
to thermal power plants as well as for meeting any contingent situations 
relating to power sector including to alleviate critical coal stock position 
in power plants. 
 
ii. An Inter -ministerial Secretary -level meeting, comprising: Secretary 
(Power), Secretary (Coal) and Chairman Railway Board, is held regularly 
to monitor coal stocks. 
 
iii. CCEA has approved the Revised SHAKTI Policy for Coal Allocation to 
Power Sector on 07.05.2025 under which interested power plants may 
participate and secure coal linkages. 
 
In respect to transmission infrastructure, Tamil Nadu is well c onnected 
to the National Grid through a robust Inter -State Transmission System (ISTS), 
comprising 765 kV and 400 kV transmission lines as well as the ±800 kV HVDC 
system, enabling reliable power transfer with other States / Regions. The 
transmission networ k is strengthened on a continuous basis in line with 
evolving power transfer requirements to ensure reliable and secure evacuation 
and supply of power. Transmission systems, wherever required, are planned 
based on generation proposals received from the Cen tral or State Sector 
through the established transmission planning process. 
……….3. 

 
 
- 3 - 
 
 
The intra state transmission system (InSTS) has already been planned for 
evacuation of power from the under-construction thermal projects viz. Ennore 
SEZ (2x660 MW) and Udangudi STPP (2x660 MW). 
 
  Environment Clearance (EC), which is granted by Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and  Climate Change (MoEF&CC), is the foremost requirement for 
establishment of new as well as expansion of thermal power capacity. All other 
clearances & permissions / approvals are processed only on the basis of grant 
of Environment Clearance; which is based on an elaborate and rigorous 
process. Further, the thermal power plants need to comply with emissions 
standards laid down by MoEF&CC, and the compliance is monitored by 
respective State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) and Central Pollution Control 
Board (CPCB).   
 
(e) : The Resource Adequacy Plan(RAP) for Tamil Nadu till 2035 -36 has been 
prepared considering demand projections that account for anticipated growth 
across all consumer sectors, including industrial, agricultural, commercial, 
domestic, and others. Based on these demand projections, the generation 
capacity addition envisaged under the RAP is likely to meet the State's 
projected electricity demand while ensuring energy security as far as 
electricity sector is concerned.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA 
REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1941 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
PROMOTION OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT 
1941.  Smt. POONAMBEN HEMATBHAI MAADAM: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken any steps to p romote digital technologies 
in water resources management and if so, the details thereof; and 
(b) whether a unified digital platform has been dev eloped for water resources 
management and monitoring and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) & (b) The Ministry of Jal Shakti has taken seve ral initiatives to promote the 
use of digital technologies and has developed vario us integrated digital 
platforms for water resources management and monito ring, across the country. 
The major initiatives, include: 
National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) has adopted  digital technologies for 
river basin planning, monitoring, project managemen t and decision support 
including: 
i. Ganga Pulse for monitoring the performance of Sewag e Treatment 
Plants (STPs) through Online Continuous Effluent Mo nitoring Systems 
(OCEMS) and manual reporting;  
ii. Drain Dashboard: A GIS-enabled platform for real-ti me monitoring of 
drains, sewage outfalls, industrial discharges and STP outlets, entering 

2 
 
the Ganga basin, facilitating pollution hotspot ide ntification and 
decision-making; 
iii. Ganga Knowledge Portal (www.gyanganga.ai): An Al-en abled knowledge 
repository providing access to research publication s, technical reports, 
river maps, datasets and decision-support resources  related to water 
resource management; 
iv. Ganga District Performance Monitoring System (GDPMS ): A web-based 
platform for monitoring the performance of District  Ganga Committees 
(DGCs), including meetings, key performance indicat ors and district-
wise progress under the Namami Gange Programme; 
v. Project Monitoring Tool (PMT): A dashboard for real -time monitoring of 
project implementation, progress, delays, MS report ing and project 
status across the Ganga basin; 
vi. Geo-PRAYAG: A GIS-based platform integrating satellite imagery, LiDAR, 
drone, hydrological, hydrogeological and other geos patial datasets to 
support river basin planning and management. 
NMCG has also developed PRAYAG (Platform for Real-t ime Analysis of 
Yamuna, Ganga and their Tributaries) under the Gang a Knowledge Centre (GKC) 
as an integrated digital platform. PRAYAG integrate s multiple digital systems, 
including Ganga Pulse, Project Monitoring Tool (PMT ), Ganga District 
Performance Monitoring System (GDPMS), Geo-PRAYAG a nd CCTV-based STP 
monitoring. The platform also integrates hydrologic al, satellite and field 
datasets, enabling real-time monitoring, GIS-based visualization, dashboard 
analytics and evidence-based decision-making for ri ver basin management. It 
provides a unified digital ecosystem for monitoring  river health, project 
implementation and pollution abatement under the Namami Gange Programme. 
Central Water Commission (CWC) has developed digita l platforms including 
the Reservoir Storage Monitoring System (RSMS) Port al to monitor live storage 

3 
 
capacity of reservoirs of the country, Project Appr aisal Management System (e-
PAMS) for online submission of project proposals, F lood Forecasting System 
through online portals (https://ffs.india-water.gov .in/ and https://aff.india-
water.gov.in/) and Flood Watch India application fo r real-time flood tracking and 
early warnings. Further, CWC also launched the C-FL OOD web-based Inundation 
Forecasting System.  
Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) has adopted advan ced digital 
technologies for efficient groundwater monitoring, assessment and management, 
including: 
i. The conventional monitoring network using water-lev el sounders is 
augmented with Automatic Digital Water Level Record ers (DWLRs). IoT-
based sensors, telemetry, GIS tools and real-time m onitoring systems 
are utilized for high-frequency monitoring and impr oved data availability 
and accuracy. DWLRs with telemetry have been instal led across the 
country for continuous monitoring of groundwater le vels. The data is 
made accessible through CGWB’s online data portal. 
ii. GRASP (Groundwater Resources Assessment for Strateg ic Planning) for 
database management and analysis of groundwater lev els, groundwater 
quality and lithological logs. 
iii. India Groundwater Resource Estimation System (IN-GR ES), a GIS-based 
web platform, for estimation of groundwater resourc es and visualization 
of assessment results. 
iv. Bhu-Neer portal, a web-based digital platform for o nline processing of 
No Objection Certificates (NOCs) applications. The portal facilitates a 
transparent and streamlined mechanism for groundwat er regulation and 
management. 
National Institute of Hydrology (NIH) has developed  digital tools such as 
KISAN SATHI/KISAN MAITRI Mobile application for irr igation management. It 
provides information regarding water availability i n reservoir, crop demand, 

4 
 
deficit in Water User Associations (WUAs) using for ecast digital data. NIH also 
developed the NIH-DHAARA (Design Hydrology and Adva nced Rainfall Analysis), 
a web-based platform for Design Flood Hydrology and Rainfall Analysis. 
The National Water Informatics Centre (NWIC) has be en established to 
facilitate collection, storage, analysis and dissem ination of water resources 
data. The Government of India has modernized surfac e water and groundwater 
monitoring networks through telemetry systems, GIS- based tools and decision 
support systems for integrated water resources management.  
Jal Shakti–Data Management System (https://jalshakt i-data.gov.in): A 
unified digital platform developed by the Governmen t of India for visualization 
and analysis of water data received from various Ce ntral and State agencies. It 
enables policymakers, researchers, and public to ex plore and analyse water-
related issues through user-friendly interfaces. 
India-WRIS (Water Resources Information System) pro vides a web-enabled 
GIS-based platform for water resources information and serves as a single-
window system for accessing, visualizing and analyz ing water resources and 
allied data for assessment, monitoring, planning and management.  
Under the Irrigation Census Scheme, implemented by Ministry of Jal 
Shakti, NIC has developed a unified digital platfor m to enable the digital data 
collection through mobile application, data validat ion and monitoring through 
web application. A dashboard showing the real time progress is also 
incorporated in the web application of the Census. 
Under Hydrology Project, a comprehensive Hydrologic al Information 
System has been established for providing scientifi cally verified, uniformly 
accepted and widely accessed hydrological records c overing all aspects of the 
hydrological cycle.  
Bharat WIN Portal is operationalized to accelerate development and 
deployment of innovative water technologies. (https://bharatwin.mowr.gov.in/)

CAUVERY-VAIGAI-GUNDAR RIVER LINK PROJECT 
1942.  Dr. GANAPATHY RAJKUMAR P: 
THIRU THANGA TAMILSELVAN: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has ever assessed the pr esent stage of 
implementation of the Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar River L ink Project and 
milestones/additional irrigation potential likely t o be created through the said 
Project in Southern Tamil Nadu for the next two years; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether the Government has ever examined the pr oject's role in 
groundwater recharge across drought-prone districts  such as Theni, 
Virudhunagar and Ramanathapuram in Tamil Nadu and i f so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government has received any request  from the State 
Government of Tamil Nadu for financial assistance f or the Cauvery-Vaigai-
Gundar Project and if so, the details thereof along  with the action taken 
thereon? 
 
 

2 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) & (b) The Cauvery–Vaigai–Gundar (CVG) Link Proj ect is one of the link 
projects identified under the National Perspective Plan. The Detailed Project 
Report (DPR) of the link was completed and circulat ed by National Water 
Development Agency (NWDA) in 2020. The project envi sages diversion of 
about 2252 MCM of water from the Kattalai Barrage o n the Cauvery River, in 
partial exchange of surplus water proposed to be re ceived in the Cauvery 
basin through the Godavari–Cauvery Link Project . 
(c) As per the DPR prepared by NWDA, the link proje ct covers drought-prone 
districts of Karur, Tiruchirappalli, Pudukkottai, S ivaganga, Ramanathapuram, 
Virudhunagar and Thoothukudi, and is expected to in directly improve 
groundwater availability by reducing dependence on groundwater for irrigation 
and supplying about 218 MCM of water for domestic a nd industrial use to 
en-route areas. However, the Central Ground Water B oard has not undertaken 
any project-specific study to assess the groundwate r-recharge impact of the 
CVG Link Project in Theni, Virudhunagar and Ramanathapuram districts.  
(d) No proposal of State Government of Tamil Nadu f or financial assistance of 
the Cauvery–Vaigai–Gundar Link Project is under con sideration of  Ministry of 
Jal Shakti.

(a) the present status and the physical progress of metro rail projects

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1944 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
INTERNATIONAL FLIGHT SERVICES FROM RAJKOT AIRPORT  
1944.    SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAI RUPALA               
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Ministry proposes to commence additional international flight services from Rajkot 
Airport and if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken in this regard; 
 
(b) whether the Ministry has taken up  the matter with the Ministry of Home Affairs for notification 
and deployment of adequate immigration facilities and manpower at Rajkot Airport and if so, the 
present status thereof; and 
 
(c) whether the Ministry has also taken up the matter with the Ministry of Finance for notification and 
deployment of adequate custom facilities and manpower at Rajkot Airport and if so, the present status 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) International flig ht operations are governed by Bilateral Air Services Agreement (ASA) between 
India and the respective countries. In accordance with respective ASAs, Indian designated carriers are 
free to mount operations to/from any point in India including Rajkot to any foreign destination as per 
mutually agreed capacity limits. However, the start of direct international flights from any point in 
India is purely a commercial decision of scheduled airlines on the basis of passenger demand, 
availability of slots, economic v iability of the route, and other associated factors. The Government 
does not interfere in the operational plans of the airlines. 
 
(b) and (c) The Ministry of Finance vide Notification dated 07.02.2025 has declared Rajkot 
International Airport as a Customs Notified Airport. Adequate Customs facilities have been 
established in the New Terminal Building. ; 
 
Further, Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has been requested to notify Rajkot International Airport as 
Immigration Check Post (ICP).

MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1945 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
RIVERBANK EROSION IN ASSAM 
1945.  Md. RAKIBUL HUSSAIN: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any study on riverbank erosion and 
land loss in Assam and if so, the details and the key findings thereof; 
(b) whether any comprehensive mitigation strategy h as been prepared to 
address riverbank erosion in the said State and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the details of the funds allocated for erosion control projects in Assam 
during the last five years? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a)   As per the morphological study of the Brahmap utra River carried out by the 
Central Water Commission (CWC) through the Indian I nstitute of Technology 
(IIT), Guwahati, it is estimated that the Brahmaput ra River underwent erosion 
of approximately 252.6 sq. km and deposition of app roximately 118.6 sq. km 
during the period from 2003-2005 and 2008-2011. 
Further, as per the study titled 
 “Identification of potential erosion sites 
based on satellite imageries for Majuli Island alon g river Brahmaputra, Assam”  
carried out by the Brahmaputra Board through the Ce ntral Water and Power 

2 
 
Research Station (CWPRS), Pune, continuous erosion near the confluence of the 
Subansiri and Brahmaputra rivers was observed throu ghout the study period 
(1986–2023). Overall, approximately 75 sq. km of la nd was eroded from various 
parts of Majuli Island, while sediment deposition o f approximately 58 sq. km 
was observed along the banks of the Brahmaputra River within Majuli Island. 
(b) & (c)   Flood management and anti-erosion schem es are formulated and 
implemented by the concerned State Governments as p er their respective 
priorities. The Union Government supplements the ef forts of the States by 
providing technical guidance and promotional financ ial assistance for flood 
management in critical areas. An integrated flood m anagement approach aims 
at adopting judicious mix of structural and non-structural measures to provide a 
reasonable degree of protection against flood damages at an economic cost.  
The Union Government is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme, 
namely, the " Flood Management and Border Areas Programme " (FMBAP) to 
provide central assistance to State Governments for  works related to flood 
control, anti-erosion, drainage development, anti-s ea erosion, etc. During the 
last five years, central assistance amounting to Rs . 342.63 crore has been 
released to the Government of Assam under the FMBAP  for flood management 
and anti-erosion projects in the State. In addition , the Brahmaputra Board has 
incurred an expenditure of Rs.109.10 crore on flood  management and anti-
erosion works in Assam during the last five years.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION 
 NO. 1947 SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH:  
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any initiative to integrate  
public transport, digital ticketing, non-motorised transport and last-mile 
connectivity through a National Smart Public Transport Mission and if 
so, the details thereof;  
(b)  whether Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) are proposed to receive financial 
and technical assistance for implementation of integrated mobility 
solutions and if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  the measures taken to reduce traffic congestion and improve urban 
mobility through digital technologies; and  
(d)  whether towns in the Bhiwani -Mahendragarh Lok Sabha Constituency 
are proposed to be included under the said initiative and if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a)  to (d): ‘Urban planning’ is a State subject, therefore, the respective 
State Governments are responsible for planning, initiating and developing 
proposal for development of urban infrastructure including p ublic transport 
project, measures to reduce congestion, improve urban mobility through 
digital technologies etc. in different cities.  
Central Government has issued various policy guidelines like National Urban 
Transport Policy 2006 and The Metro Policy 2017 for systematic planning 
and execution of Public Transport project including metro project, which are 
applicable to all regions of India. 
As on date, per se there is no National Smart Public Transport S cheme for 
integrated public transport, digital ticketing, non- motorized transport, last-
mile connectivity.  
…2/- 

-2- 
However, Central Government considers Central Financial Assistance, for 
deployment of e- buses under various Central Schemes (PM e- Bus Sewa, PM 
e- Drive etc.) and for implementation of Metro projects as and when posed 
by concerned State Government . Under above interventions digital 
ticketing, integrated public Transport etc. are priority items.  
National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) is an interoperable card with vision 
of “One Nation, One Card” , which works seamlessly among different 
Metro/RRTS and Bus operators. The Ministry has issued directions for 
implementation of National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) ecosystem based 
on qSPARC (quick Specification for Payment Application of RuPay Chip) 
developed by National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It is functional 
in 13 Metro projects and 11 Bus Transport corporations by ensuring ease of 
ticketing through these digital technologies , which facilitates shift from 
private vehicle to public transport thereby reducing traffic congestion.  
Further, PM-eBus Sewa Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Housing and 
Urban Affairs includes implementation of NCMC based Automatic Fare 
Collection System (AFCS) for bus operations. 
Further, under “Transport Planning and Capacity Building in Urban Transport 
for metro and non metro projects” sub scheme of MoHUA, various studies 
like preparation of Integrated Mobility Plan, Detailed Project Reports, Multi 
Modal integration plans etc. have been eligible components for Central 
Finance Assistance for cities, ULBs etc.  which is considered based on 
feasibility of proposal as and when posed by concerned State Government.

Cleaning and rejuvenation of rivers is an ongoing p rocess. It is the responsibility 
of States/Union Territories (UTs), local bodies and  industries to ensure required 
treatment of sewage and industrial effluents before  discharging into rivers and other 
water bodies, land or coastal waters for prevention  and control of pollution therein. 
This Ministry of Jal Shakti provides financial and technical assistance to States/UTs 
through the Central Sector Scheme of Namami Gange Programme for river Ganga and 
its tributaries and the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the National River 
Conservation Plan (NRCP) for Other River Basins. Ap art from this, sewerage 
infrastructure is created under programs like Atal Mission for Rejuvenation & Urban 
Transformation (AMRUT) and Smart Cities Mission of Ministry of Housing & Urban

are encouraged to minimize wastewater generation th rough technological 
upgradation, reuse and recycling of wastewater and to maintain Zero Liquid 
Discharge, wherever feasible.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1951 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
 
 SALIENT FEATURES OF PMKSY 
 
1951. SHRI ANURAG SHARMA: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the salient features, objectives and progress made under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) in developing modern food processing infrastructure, 
integrated cold chain facilities, agro-processing clusters and value addition units 
across the country; 
(b)  the details of projects sanctioned, completed and operational under the scheme during 
the last three years along with the investment leveraged and employment generated, 
State-wise; 
(c)  the measures taken to reduce post-harvest losses, strengthen Farmer Producer 
Organisations (FPOs), promote food processing at the farm-gate level and enhance 
farmers' income; 
(d)  whether the Government has assessed the impact of the scheme on food processing 
capacity, exports and reduction of wastage and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  the steps being taken to expand the scheme in aspirational and agricultural regions 
including Bundelkhand to promote value addition, rural entrepreneurship and 
employment generation? 
ANSWER  
  
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
 
(a): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing a central 
sector umbrella scheme called “Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY)” since 2017-
18 across the country. The salient features of PMKSY are as follows: 
 
(i)  Development of integrated food processing and preservation infrastructure across the 
value chain from farm gate to retail; 
(ii) Promotion of value addition and reduction of post-harvest losses; 
(iii) Financial assistance for creation/expansion of food processing and preservation 
capacities; 
(iv) Development of integrated cold chain and value addition infrastructure; 
(v) Strengthening of food safety and quality assurance infrastructure; 
(vi) Promotion of private investment in the food processing sector; 
(vii) Generation of employment and enhancement of farmers' income through improved 
market linkages; and 
(viii) Promotion of export competitiveness of processed food products. 

The objective of PMKSY is to ensure overall development of the food processing 
sector by incentivizing the creation of modern food processing and preservation infrastructure 
across the country. The scheme presently comprises six on-going component schemes and two 
discontinued component schemes (w.e.f. 01.04.2021). The component-wise progress under 
PMKSY is placed at Annexure I. 
 
(b): The State-wise details of projects sanctioned, completed and operational under 
PMKSY during the last three years along with investment leveraged and employment generated 
are at Annexure II. 
 
(c) : The component schemes under PMKSY provide financial assistance in the form of 
grants-in-aid/subsidy for creation of modern food processing and preservation infrastructure with 
the objective of reducing post-harvest losses and enhancing value addition. The creation of food 
processing infrastructure enhances demand for agricultural produce, leading to better price 
realization and improved income for farmers. As on 30.06.2026, 1256 projects are operational 
under PMKSY, benefiting about 37.76 lakh farmers. PMKSY is a demand-driven scheme and 
applications are invited from eligible applicants, including Farmers Producer Organisation 
(FPOs) through Expressions of Interest (EoIs). To strengthen farmer–producer linkages, PMKSY 
provides enhanced financial assistance to FPOs with loan requirement and a reduced net-worth 
requirement compared to the general category applicants. 
Further, under the centrally sponsored PMFME scheme of the Ministry, FPOs are eligible for 
35% credit-linked subsidy up to ₹10 lakh for setting up or upgrading micro-food processing 
enterprises, 35% grant of up to ₹3 crore for establishing Common Infrastructure and Branding & 
Marketing support in terms of grant upto 50% for groups of FPOs, at State/regional level. 
 
(d): The Government regularly monitors the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan 
SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY). As on 30.06.2026, 1735 projects have been approved under 
PMKSY, of which 1256 projects are operational, creating 294.21 LMT per annum of processing 
and preservation capacity. The creation of this infrastructure has enhanced value addition, 
strengthened the food processing ecosystem, improved supply chain efficiency, reduced post-
harvest losses through the capacities created under completed projects, and contributed to the 
growth of the food processing sector and exports of processed food products. 
 
(e) : Under PMKSY, the Ministry provides financial assistance to eligible applicant 
organizations/entities/entrepreneurs including rural entrepreneurs for setting up/expansion of 
eligible projects. PMKSY is a demand-driven scheme. The funds are not 
allocated/sanctioned/released State-wise under any of the component schemes of PMKSY. 
Applications are invited through Expressions of Interest (EoIs) from all over India, including 
aspirational and agricultural regions such as Bundelkhand. The proposals received are scrutinized 
for eligibility and evaluated as per the applicable scheme guidelines. Financial assistance is 
provided to eligible projects approved on merit, subject to availability of funds. Through the 
creation of modern food processing infrastructure, PMKSY promotes value addition of 
agricultural produce, encourages rural entrepreneurship, generates employment opportunities, 
and enhances income opportunities for farmers.

EXPANSION OF PNG INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
1952. SHRI B K PARTHASARATHI: 
 
पेटŌ ोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps taken for expansion of Piped Natural Gas (PNG) infrastructure across the country, 
including the criteria adopted for prioritisation of areas and the list of districts identified or prioritised 
for PNG expansion; 
(b) the number of States and Union Territories that have constituted Quick Response Teams (QRTs) 
or Task Forces, State/UT-wise; 
(c) whether the Government is monitoring the preparation and maintenance of databases of certified 
plumbers by the States and Union Territories for PNG deployment and maintenance, if so the details 
of the States and union Territories that have prepared such databases, State/UT-wise; 
(d) the details of the targets fixed for establishing new PNG connections and the number of 
connections achieved against such targets, State/UT-wise; and 
(e) whether the Government has identified any shortage of trained manpower for the expansion, 
operation and maintenance of PNG infrastructure, if so, the details thereof along with the measures 
taken to address such shortages, including skilling initiatives, certification programmes, industry 
partnerships and training targets? 
 
ANSWER 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी ) 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (e) Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections is part of the development of City Gas 
Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter alia include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other 
facilities for the supply of PNG to domestic, commercial and industrial units. This is being carried 
out by entities authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). After 
completion of 12/12A CGD bidding round, PNGRB has authorized entities for the development of 
CGD network in 309 Geographical Areas (GAs), covering the entire mainland area of the country. 
As on 31.05.2026, the authorized CGD entities have provided 1,70,69,775 PNG (D) connections 
across the country against the Minimum Work Programme (MWP) targets of 12,65,41,862 PNG 
(D) connections to be achieved by 2034. CGD infrastructure rollout is undertaken by the 
authorized entities in accordance with the authorization granted by PNGRB and the approved 
project plan. The State/UT wise PNG (D) connections progress, as on 31.05.2026, is at 
Annexure-I. 

PNGRB, in collaboration with CGD entities, launched the National PNG Drive 2.0 from 1st 
January 2026 to 30th June 2026. PNGRB has informed that the initiative aims to ensure optimal 
utilization of existing infrastructure, promote new connections and activate non-billed customers, 
with an overall objective to increase the usage of natural gas across the diverse user categories. 
Under the initiative, various measures have been implemented by the Government and 
authorized CGD entities, including: 
i. Expansion of PNG connectivity to households, commercial establishments and industries; 
ii. Conversion of connected households into active billed consumers; 
iii. Awareness campaigns and consumer outreach programmes; 
iv. Coordination with State Governments and local authorities for expeditious statutory 
permissions; and 
v. Implementation of consumer-friendly measures, including digital registration, simplified 
connection processes and promotional schemes offered by CGD entities. 
The Government has notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under the 
Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure 
across the country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework for grant of right 
of way (RoW) and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case 
of delays, and prohibiting imposition of unauthorized charges by public authorities. It also 
addresses access issues in residential and private areas by ensuring non-discriminatory and time-
bound permissions, thereby removing key bottlenecks in pipeline laying. In pursuance thereof, 
19 States/UTs have appointed Nodal Officers. 
As per the available information, 3 states namely Assam, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh have 
maintained and shared the database of ITI plumbers with CGD entities through their education 
institutes. Further, the Ministry is taking proactive measures to augment the availability of 
skilled manpower required for expansion, operation and maintenance of PNG infrastructure. 
These include: 
i. Training of plumbers through the Skill Development Council and authorized CGD 
entities; 
ii. Master Trainer Orientation Programme on CGD in collaboration with the Ministry of 
Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and the Government of Maharashtra, 
under which around 100 Master Trainers have been trained with a target of training about 
100 plumbers by each Master Trainer; 
iii. Engagement of trained fitters/plumbers based on lists shared by MSDE; and 
iv. Capacity-building and skill development programmes being conducted by individual 
CGD entities for developing skilled plumbers required for PNG network expansion and 
maintenance.

(b) the number of individual and community forest rights titles distributed under the Forest Rights Act,

 (c) whether the Government has assessed issues relating to land alienation, malnutrition and 
displacement among tribal communities in Kerala, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the funds allocated and released to Kerala under the Tribal Sub-Plan and other centrally sponsored 
schemes during the last five years, year-wise; and 
 
(e) whether the Government proposes any special intervention for improving health, education and 
livelihood opportunities for tribal communities in Kerala, if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS  
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
a. As per Census 2011, the Scheduled Tribe (ST) population of Kerala is 4,84,839, constituting 1.45 per 
cent of the total population of the State. The districts having the highest Scheduled Tribe population 
are Wayanad, Idukki, Palakkad, Kasaragod and Kannur.       
b. The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 
is implemented by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, while the 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs monitors its implementation through Monthly Progress Reports received from 
them. As per MPR of MoTA, 2,923 Individual Forest Rights (IFR) titles and 110 Community Forest 
Rights (CFR) titles, aggregating 3033 forest rights titles, have been distributed under the Act.  
c. The Government accords high priority to the socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes, 
including those residing in Kerala. Issues relating to land rights, education, health, nutrition and 
livelihood are addressed through implementation of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and various schemes 
of the Central and State Governments. Matters relating to land alienation are dealt with by the State 
Government under the applicable State laws, while health and nutrition interventions are implemented 
through convergence under various Central and State Government programmes. 
d. The year wise details of funds released to the Government of Kerala under Tribal sub Plan and other 
centrally sponsored schemes:

e. The government continues to support the welfare and development of Scheduled tribes in Kerala 
through various interventions: 
i. Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan: Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram 
Utkarsh Abhiyan Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 
2nd October, 2024. The Abhiyan comprises of 25 interventions implemented by 17-line Ministries 
and aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, provide social infrastructure like hostels, 
Anganwadi facilities and mobile medical units and set up Van Dhan Vikas Kendras to provide 
livelihood opportunities benefiting more than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 
States/UTs in 5 years. The Abhiyan has a total budgetary outlay of Rs.79,156 Cr (Central share: 
₹56,333 Cr and State share: ₹22,823 Cr) 
ii. Pre-Matric Scholarships to ST students: The scheme is applicable to students who are studying 
in Classes IX –X. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per 
annum. Scholarship of Rs.225/-per month for day scholars and Rs.525/-per month for hostellers is 
given for a period of 10 months in a year. Scholarship is disbursed through the State Government/UT 
Administration. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except North East 
and Hills States/UT like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 
90:10.For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share. 
iii. Post Matric Scholarship to ST students: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial 
assistance to the Scheduled Tribe students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary levels 
to enable them to complete their education. Parental income from all sources should not be more 
than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Compulsory fees charged by educational institutions are reimbursed 
subject to the limit fixed by the concerned State Fee fixation committee and scholarship amount of 
Rs.230 to Rs.1200 per month, depending upon the course of study is paid. The Scheme is 
implemented by the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Funding ratio is 75:25 
between Centre and States for all States except NE and Hilly States/UT of Himachal Pradesh, 
Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing pattern 
is 100% Central share. 

iv. National Scholarship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students (earlier known as Top 
Class Scholarship Scheme): Under this Scheme, Scholarship is provided for pursuing 
Graduate/Post Graduate courses in the selected top-class Government and Non-Government 
Institutes in professional fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information 
Technology, Law etc. All the ST students, with annual parental income is not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs 
and studying in the 265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are eligible to receive scholarship. This 
scheme is started from year 2007-08 (b) National Fellowship Scheme for Higher Education of 
ST Students: It is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs to grant 
scholarship to meritorious ST students for pursuing Ph.D in India after completion of Master degree. 
This scheme is started from year 2005-06. The total number of fresh fellowships for Ph.D every year 
will be 750. ST students with a minimum of 55% marks in Master Degree up to the age of 36 years 
are eligible to apply for fellowship under the Scheme. The value of fellowship is at par with UGC 
rates. 
v. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students: It is a Central Sector Scheme of Ministry of 
Tribal Aﬀairs under which scholarships are given to the meritorious Schedule Tribe (ST) students 
for pursuing higher education in top 1000 ranked (as per latest QS world ranking) 
Institutes/Universities abroad. This scheme is started from year 1954-55. The Scheme is 
implemented through the Indian Embassies/Missions abroad, Ministry of External Aﬀairs. Twenty 
awards are given every year. ST students with annual family income not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs are 
eligible to apply for the Scholarship under the Scheme. 
vi. Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN): Government launched 
Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for socio-economic 
development of 75 PVTG communities residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide 
basic facilities such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health 
and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and 
sustainable livelihood opportunities in 3 years. These objectives are planned to be met through 11 
interventions including Hostels and Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) implemented by 9-line Ministries. 
PM JANMAN has total budgetary outlay of Rs.24,104 Cr (Central share: ₹15336 Cr and State share: 
₹8768 Cr). 
vii. Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution: Under the Proviso to Article 275(1) of 
Constitution, Grants are released to States, having ST population for raising the level of 
administration in Scheduled Areas and for the welfare of tribal people. This is a Special Area 
Programme and 100% grants are provided to States. Funds are released to the State Governments 
depending on the felt needs of ST population to bridge the gap in infrastructure activities in the fields 
of education, health, skill development, livelihood, drinking water, sanitation, etc. 
viii. Grant-in Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes: Under 
the scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, 
the Ministry funds projects in the fields of education and health, covering residential schools, non-
residential schools, hostels, mobile dispensaries, ten or more bedded hospitals, livelihood, etc. 
ix. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): The Scheme provides quality residential education 
to Scheduled Tribe students in remote and tribal areas with the objective of enabling them to access 
quality education comparable to the best institutions in the country. The schools provide modern 
educational infrastructure along with facilities for holistic development of tribal students. 
x. Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM): The Mission promotes sustainable livelihoods 
of Scheduled Tribes through value addition, entrepreneurship development, marketing support and 
strengthening of tribal producer organisations, with emphasis on value chains based on Minor Forest 
Produce and other tribal products. 
xi. Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE): The Scheme 
supports Tribal Research Institutes for research, documentation, capacity building, preservation and 

promotion of tribal culture, awareness generation, information dissemination and evidence-based 
policy support. 
xii. National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC): under the 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs is an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of 
Scheduled Tribes implements various schemes for livelihood generation. NSTFDC extends 
concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe communities. 
xiii. Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST): The Scheme is implemented through the 
National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) to provide 
concessional venture capital assistance to Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs for establishment and 
expansion of income-generating enterprises. 
xiv. Strengthening of health, education, drinking water, connectivity and other infrastructure through 
convergence with Ministries/Departments and the Government of Kerala.

LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1954  
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30th July, 2026 
 
STRENGTHENING INDIA'S ENERGY SECURITY AND INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
1954. SMT. ROOPKUMARI CHOUDHARY: 
 
पेटŌ ोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũी 
 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any measures to strengthen India's natural gas 
infrastructure and energy security in view of recent global supply disruptions; 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the progress made in expanding City Gas Distribution (CGD) 
networks, pipeline infrastructure and Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connectivity, State/UT- wise; 
(c) the steps taken to enhance domestic production of crude oil and natural gas, reduce import 
dependence and strengthen strategic petroleum reserves; 
(d) whether any financial or policy support has been extended to expedite CGD infrastructure and 
improve last-mile PNG connectivity, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the roadmap of the Government for increasing the share of natural gas in India's energy mix 
while ensuring affordable, reliable and uninterrupted supply across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
पेटŌोिलयम और Ůाक ृ ितक गैस मंũालय मŐ राǛ मंũी 
(ŵी सुरेश गोपी )  
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  
(SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
 
(a) to (e) The Government have taken various steps to strengthen the Natural gas infrastructure 
which inter-alia, include setting up of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) import and regasification 
infrastructure, expansion of National Gas Grid Pipeline and expansion of City Gas Distribution 
(CGD) network.  
Further, to strengthen energy security and minimise supply risks, India has significantly diversified 
its energy supplies. LNG sourcing has expanded from 6 countries to 15 countries. This 
diversification has reduced dependence on any particular country, region or transit route and 
enhanced India's ability to manage supply disruptions and market volatility. Government, in 
consultation with Public Sector Oil and Gas Companies and other stakeholders, continuously 
assesses global supply conditions and takes appropriate action to ensure uninterrupted availability 
of LNG. 
In order to deal with the middle east crisis, the Government also notified the Natural Gas (Supply 
Regulation) Order, 2026 on 09.03.2026 under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to regulate the 
production, allocation and distribution of natural gas and to ensure its equitable availability. The 

Order accorded priority in the allocation of natural gas to critical sectors, including PNG 
(Domestic) (100% of the average consumption during the preceding six months), CNG (Transport), 
LPG production and fertilizer, thereby ensuring continuity of essential services, energy security and 
public welfare. The said measures were temporary in nature and, in view of the improvement in the 
supply situation, were withdrawn vide notification dated 04.07.2026.  
Providing Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections and establishment of Compressed Natural Gas 
(CNG) stations is part of the development of City Gas Distribution (CGD) Network, which inter-
alia include creation of pipeline infrastructure and other facilities for the supply of PNG to 
domestic, commercial and industrial units and CNG to transport sector is being carried out by the 
entities authorized by Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB). The state-wise CGD 
progress, as on 31.05.2026, is at Annexure. 
The investment to develop the CGD network is made by authorized entity in accordance with the 
authorization by PNGRB and approved work programme. No funds are sanctioned or allocated by 
Government for implementation of the CGD project. 
The Government has undertaken a series of comprehensive policy, regulatory and fiscal measures 
to boost domestic crude oil and natural gas production and reduce dependency on imports with the 
objective of strengthening the country’s energy security and reducing foreign exchange expenditure 
through participation by both public and private sector companies, which, inter-alia, include 
reforms viz. legislative changes through the Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment 
Act, removal of No-Go restrictions in the country’s offshore areas, transition from Production 
Sharing Contracts (PSCs) to Revenue Sharing Contracts (RSCs), massive investment in acquisition 
and processing of seismic data, increase in number of exploratory wells drilled etc. During the last 
decade over 3.5 lakh sq km of exploration acreages have been awarded. 
Government, through a Special Purpose Vehicle called Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserve Limited 
(ISPRL), have also established Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR) facilities to act as buffer for 
short-term supply shocks. Under Phase-I, SPRs have been established at 3 locations in Andhra 
Pradesh and Karnataka with a total capacity of 5.33 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) of crude oil. In 
July 2021, Government had also approved the establishment of two additional commercial cum-
strategic petroleum reserve facilities with total storage capacity of 6.5 MMT in Odisha and 
Karnataka, under Phase-II of the SPR program. 
Besides strengthening the natural gas infrastructure, Government has undertaken many steps to 
increase the share of natural gas in India’s energy mix and ensure affordable, reliable and 
uninterrupted supply which include allocation of domestic gas to Compressed Natural Gas 
(Transport)/ Piped Natural Gas (Domestic) CNG (T)/PNG(D) on priority, allowing marketing and 
pricing freedom with a ceiling price to gas produced from high pressure/high temperature areas, 
deep water & ultradeep water and from coal seams, Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable 
Transportation (SATAT) initiative to promote Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) etc. 
 
 

The Government has notified a comprehensive control order dated 24.03.2026 under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 to facilitate time-bound expansion of pipeline infrastructure across the 
country, especially CGD. The Order provides a uniform framework for grant of right of way (RoW) 
and permissions by mandating strict timelines, enabling deemed approvals in case of delays, and 
prohibiting imposition of unauthorized charges by public authorities. It also addresses access issues 
in residential and private areas by ensuring non-discriminatory and time-bound permissions, 
thereby removing key bottlenecks in pipeline laying.

interventions under PM-JANMAN have improved access to housing, healthcare,

Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in Kerala and if so, the details and findings

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. - 1956 
ANSWERED ON 30th JULY, 2026 
  
ELECTRIC VEHICLES 
  
1956.  SHRI KAMAKHYA PRASAD TASA: 
   
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether it is a fact that electric vehicles are increasing day by day 
because of less pollution and lower running costs, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that public charging stations for electric 
vehicles are fewer, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the number of registered electric vehicles and electric vehicle 
public charging stations in the country; 
(d) whether the Government is aware t hat the owners of electric 
vehicles have expressed their concern regarding not having enough 
charging stations particularly on the State and National Highways, if 
so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government has issued instructions for the provi sion 
of electric vehicle service charging points in all major locations in 
towns, cities and on highways and is there any specific plan for 
setting up of more charging stations for electric vehicles in Assam, if 
so, the details thereof? 

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
                                                                                         
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) Electric Vehicles are increasing due to their lower operational 
costs and zero tailpipe emissions as co mpared to Internal Combustion 
Engine (ICE) vehicles. VAHAN data indicates that EV penetration in 
India has grown from 0.71% in Financial Year 2019 -20 to 8.26% in FY 
2025-26.  
(b) to (d) Private sector is free to take up installation of EV Charging 
Stations (EVCS) as per the Government in Ministry of Power (MoP)'s 
Guidelines of September 17, 2024.  
Government in Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) is promoting setting 
up Electric Vehicle Public Charging Station (EVPCS) through Faster 
Adoption and Manufacturin g of Electric Vehicles (FAME -II) & Prime 
Minister's Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement 
(PM E -DRIVE) schemes. Rs.912.50 crore were allocated under the 
FAME-II Scheme for setting up of EVPCS on pan India basis. Further, 
MHI has also made an allocation of Rs. 2,000 Crore under the PM E -
DRIVE scheme, for deployment of adequate number of EVPCS on a 
pan-India basis, including State and National highways.  
As per VAHAN data, the total number of EVs (as on 26 -07-2026) is 
1,00,23,396 for all categories of vehicles. 
As per data received from Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) 
portal there are 52,718 EV Charging stations in the country as on 
31.03.2026. 

(e)  "Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Electric Vehicle 
Charging Infrastructure-2024" have been issued to ensure a connected 
and interoperable network. 
As per information received from 3 Oil Marketing Companies namely 
Bharat petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Indian Oil Corporation 
Limited (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corpor ation Limited (HPCL), 
under the FAME-II scheme, a total of 117 EVPCS have been sanctioned 
for Assam, out of which 88 EVPCS are operational as on 01.07.2026.   
National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) envisions development of 
wayside amenities through Na tional Highways Logistics Management 
Limited (NHLML) at approximate interval of 40 -60 kms along National 
Highways and Expressways for providing public facilities like eateries, 
toilet, drinking water, parking, Fuelling Stations, EV charging stations, 
short term accommodation, etc. to the road users and truckers. As on 
date, 3 WSA sites provisioned with EV charging facility are operational 
in the state of Assam. 
Further, no proposal has been received from Assam under the PM E -
DRIVE scheme.

ALIGNMENT OF GORAKHPUR-SILIGURI EXPRESSWAY 
  
1957.  SMT. LOVELY ANAND: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government is aware that a large number of residential and 
commercial properties are being affected by the present alignment of the 
proposed Gorakhpur -Siliguri Expressway near Dhankaul Chowk in Sheohar 
district of Bihar; 
(b) whether it is a fact that the alternative alignment of the expressway was 
proposed from south of Dhankaul Dam in the survey of December, 2025, 
which would have minimized loss and displacement of the people; 
(c) if so, the reasons for change in the present alignment; and 
(d) whether the Government is likely to consider revising the route keeping in 
view the local public interest, minimum displacement and the earlier 
proposed alignment and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (d) Alignment of Gorakhpur Siliguri  Access Controlled High Speed 
Greenfield corridor has been finalised after detailed analysis of options and 
stakeholder consultation process. The State Government has also consented 
to the alignment after due deliberations. Further, a specialized five -member 
committee conducted physical inspections including locations in the 
Sheohar district to map out land types, residential structures, and 
commercial setups directly on the alignment path. 

  
The alignment of Gorakhpur-Siliguri Access Controlled High Speed Greenfield 
corridor was approved in the Alignment Approval Committee in its meeting 
held on 04.04.2025. However, it was noticed that the proposed alignment 
near Sheohar is overlapping with the new proposed Railway line and to avoid 
conflict with Railway li ne, minor re -alignment has been proposed near 
Dhankaul Dham. However, care has been taken to minimize acquisition of 
residential or commercial structures.

INTEGRATION OF NAVIC AND GAGAN NAVIGATION SYSTEMS  
1959.    SHRI DUSHYANT SINGH                      
 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government is integrating India's indigenous satellite navigation 
systems namely NavIC and GAGAN with the expanding aviation infrastructure 
to enhance navigation precision, air traffic management and saf er aircraft 
operations and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of the coverage range and operational capabilities of NavIC and 
GAGAN for civilian aviation including their use in approach procedures, 
runway navigation and aircraft tracking particula rly at newly developed and 
regional airports; 
(c) the steps taken to integrate these systems with national air traffic 
management systems, logistics hubs and multimodal transport networks; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to expand the use of satell ite-based 
augmentation systems for performance -based navigation and satellite -guided 
landing procedures especially at smaller airports under the Regional 
Connectivity Scheme-UDAN and if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a): NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation), developed by Indian Space 
Research Organisation (ISRO), is an indigenous regional satellite navigation 
system currently being utilized for non -civil aviation appli cations and is not 
integrated with aviation infrastructure. GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented 
Navigation) is India's Satellite -Based Augmentation System (SBAS), jointly 
developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the Airports 
Authority of I ndia (AAI), integrated with aviation infrastructure to enhance 
navigation precision, air traffic management and safer aircraft operations. 
 

(b) to (d):  Director General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has certified GAGAN 
for Required Navigation Performance (RN P-0.1) enroute operations across 
Indian Flight Information Regions (FIRs) and for Approach with Vertical 
Guidance (APV -1) services at airports with published approach procedure 
charts, enabling precision approach and landing for suitably equipped aircraft. 
  
GAGAN supports Performance -Based Navigation (PBN) and satellite guided 
landing procedures. At present, 23 GAGAN-based landing approach procedures 
have been published for 15 airports across India including 09 airports 
operationalised under UDAN, namely Kadapa, Kishangarh, Deoghar, Jalgaon, 
Kandla, Belagavi, Porbandar, Pantnagar and Kolhapur where suitably equipped 
aircraft can utilise these procedures.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1960 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
  
ERNAKULAM BYPASS PROJECT 
  
1960. SHRI HIBI EDEN: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government has identified and implemented specific 
measures to expedite the Ernakulam Bypass project, if so, the details thereof 
and if not, the reasons therefor; 
  
(b) whether the Government is aware that the commencement of work on the 
Ernakulam Bypass is facing uncertainty, if so, the details thereof and if not, 
the reasons therefor; 
  
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of these delays on the 
overall timeline of the Ernakulam Bypass project, if so, the details thereof 
and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
  
(d) whether the Government has undertaken or proposes to undertake a 
detailed review of the alignment of the Ernakulam Bypass particularly with 
regard to en suring seamless connectivity to  Cochin International Airport at 
the starting point and minimizing the impact on densely populated 
habitations near Kundanoor at the end, if so, the details thereof and if not, 
the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (d) The project for Ernakulam Bypass was initially proposed to start 
from NH-544 at Angamaly and terminate at Nettoor on NH-66. 
  

The alignment of the project was considered by Alignment App raisal 
Committee (AAC) and certain modifications were advised.   The revised 
alignment (49.5 Km.) proposal avoiding major builtup areas including 
Kudanoor was considered and approved by AAC in June, 2026.   Modified 
alignment of this bypass starts near Kochi  Airport and connect to Aroor – 
Thuravoor Elevated Corridor on NH 66.  
  
The further process of Detailed Project Report (DPR) after the alignment 
finalisation has been taken up, upon completion of which, the appraisal and 
approval shall be initiated depend ing upon traffic density, techno -economic 
feasibility and synergy with priority of PM Gati-Shakti.

UNIVERSAL COVERAGE UNDER JJM 
 
1962. SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether all rural households have been provided Functional Household Tap Connections 
(FHTCs) under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) if not, the details of uncovered households, State-wise; and 
(c) the expected timeline for achieving universal coverage under the mission? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
(a) to (c) Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States, is implementing 
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)-Har Ghar Jal to enable every rural household in the country to have 
assured potable water through tap connection at a service level of 55 litre per capita per day 
(LPCD), of prescribed quality (BIS:10500), on regular and long-term basis. The Union Cabinet 
has approved the extension of the JJM 2.0 by December, 2028 with an enhanced outlay and a 
restructured implementation framework focusing on structural reforms in rural drinking water 
supply sector. 
Drinking water is a  State subject, and hence, the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation, and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including those 
under the Jal Jeevan Mission, lies with the respective State/UT Governments. The Government 
of India supports the States by providing technical and financial assistance only. 
At the start of the Mission, only 3.24 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported to have 
tap water connection in the country. As on 18.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural househol ds, 
around 15.89 crore (82.09%) rural households have been provided tap water connection. The 
State-wise details of Household tap water connections is at Annexure.

CHAUSA-VARANASI FOUR-LANE HIGHWAY 
  
1963.  SHRI SUDHAKAR SINGH: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government has initiated or conducted any 
proposal, survey, or feasibility study for the construction of a four -
lane National Highway from Chausa in Buxar district of Bihar to 
Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is a fact that the Chausa -Varanasi route holds 
immense significance from a religious, cultural, commercial and 
traffic perspective and that the existing narrow road currently leads 
to frequent traffic cong estion, accidents and substantial loss of 
time; 
(c) whether a survey has been conducted or a proposal initiated and 
the current status, estimated cost, progress of land acquisition and 
the tentative timeline for the commencement and completion of its 
construction, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government is contemplating upon granting 
approval to the Chausa -Varanasi four -lane highway on a priority
