UPPER INDRAVATI PROJECT 
1964. Shri SAPTAGIRI SANKAR ULAKA: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that Nabarangpu r district of Odisha has remained 
largely deprived of irrigation benefits despite con tributing substantially to the Upper 
Indravati Project and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the original Detailed Project Report (D PR), the 1975 Indravati Water 
Agreement and World Bank-assisted project documents  envisaged irrigation, 
downstream water utilisation or the other benefits for Nabarangpur and Koraput 
districts and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the prescribed minimum downstream relea se of seven cumecs of water is 
being maintained and monitored and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has received any proposa l from the State Government of 
Odisha for providing irrigation to Nabarangpur by u tilising Upper Indravati waters and if 
so, the details and the status thereof; and 
(e) the Central assistance sanctioned during the la st ten years for such irrigation 
projects and the steps proposed to be taken to ensu re equitable distribution of 
irrigation benefits? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 

2 
 
(a)        Water, being State subject, irrigation p rojects are planned, funded, executed 
and maintained by the State Governments themselves as per their own resources and 
priorities. 
As per information provided by the Government of Od isha, out of the 1.85 lakh 
hectares of available cultivable area in the Nabara ngpur district, an irrigation potential 
of approx. 1.26 lakh hectares has been created upto  March 2026.  Government of 
Odisha is implementing various irrigation projects in the Nabarangpur district.  These 
include Turi-Guntat Irrigation Project to irrigate about 9135 hectares, two Mega Lift 
clusters to create an irrigation potential of 19247  hectares and four Low Height 
Storage Structures (LHSS) with a total potential ayacut of 2000 hectares. 
(b)        As informed by the Government of Odisha,  the original Detailed Project Report, 
the 1975 Indravati Water Agreement and World Bank a ssisted project documents 
envisaged irrigation development and downstream wat er utilisation benefit for Koraput 
& Nabarangpur districts.  The State Government has taken up schemes like Mega Lift, 
CAPEX etc. in accordance with these provisions. 
 (c)        As informed by the Government of Odisha , the prescribed minimum 
downstream release of seven cumecs of water is being maintained and monitored. 
(d)       A proposal for the Nabarangpur Irrigation  Project was received by the Central 
Water Commission (CWC) for technical examination. F ollowing its initial examination, 
the CWC requested the Government of Odisha to furni sh a No objection Certificate 
(NoC) from the Government of Chhattisgarh. However,  as requisite NoC was not 
received, the project proposal was returned to the Government of Odisha on 
31.01.2024. 
(e)     Eight (08) major & medium irrigation projec ts in Odisha, including the Upper 
Indravati project, were included under Pradhan Mant ri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana - 
Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (PMKSY-AIB P) with total central assistance 
of Rs. 1442.85 crore. Central assistance amounting to Rs. 1208.86 crore has been 
released to these projects during the last 10 years , out of which Rs. 18 crore was 
provided to the Upper Indravati project.

Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) the major achievements of the Smart Cities Mission (SCM) in 
Madhya Pradesh, city -wise including projects completed, 
expenditure incurred and the key urban outcomes; 
(b) the status of the remaining projects in the State along with the 
expected timeline for their completion; 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any outcome 
assessment, third- party evaluation or post -implementation 
impact study to assess improvements in mobility, public 
services, governance and quality of life under the SCM and if so, 
the details thereof, city-wise; and 
(d) the status of expenditure, physical progress and expected 
outcomes of SCM projects in Satna, project -wise, if any, along 
with the mechanisms adopted to ensure timely implementation,  
quality standards and efficient utilisation of public funds? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (d) : In the State of Madhya Pradesh, 07 cities, 
viz. Bhopal, 
Gwalior, Indore, Jabalpur, Sagar, Satna and Ujjain have been selected.

projects amounting to ₹15,129 Cr, 778 projects (98% of total projects) 
amounting to ₹14,612 Cr have been completed. The State has been 
able to claim its entire Central Financial Assistance of ₹3,430 Cr, out 
of which ₹3,422 Cr (99%) has been utilized. The details of projects and

environmental outcomes.  
 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has a multi -level 
review structure to expedite the progress of projects under the SCM. 
At the National level, implementation is monitored by an Apex 
Committee headed by Secretary, MoHUA.  At the State level, Mission 
implementation is monitored by the State level High Powered Steering 
Committee (HPSC) chaired by the Chief Secretary.  At the City level, 
there is provision for establishing Smart City Advisory Forum (SCAF) 
for all 100 cities to advise and enable collaboration among various 
stakeholders.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1967 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
 
 MEGA FOOD PARKS AND FOOD PROCESSING PROJECTS 
 
1967. DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN: 
SHRI RAJESH RANJAN: 
SHRI KONDA VISHWESHWAR REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of Mega Food Parks, food processing projects/units, Agro Processing 
Clusters and Cold Chain projects approved and sanctioned during the last five years, 
State-wise, including in Bihar and Telangana; 
(b)  the total amount disbursed/assistance released and utilized for these projects, State 
and district-wise, including Bihar and Telangana; 
(c)  the steps taken to promote exports of processed food, value addition, reduce post-
harvest losses and generate employment; 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to set up Mega Food Parks, Food Processing 
Clusters or Cold Chain Projects in Bihar particularly in the Kosi-Seemanchal region 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  whether any proposals from the State Government of Telangana are pending with 
the Ministry and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER  
  
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
 
(a) & (b):  The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) provides financial assistance 
for setting up food processing projects under the Central Sector umbrella scheme Pradhan 
Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) across the country. The State-wise and district-
wise details of food processing projects/ units, Agro Processing Clusters and Cold Chain
 projects approved/sanctioned during the last five years, including in Bihar and Telangana, 
along with the amount of grants-in-aid released and utilized, are placed at the Annexure. The 
Mega Food Park component of PMKSY has been discontinued with effect from 01.04.2021. 
 
(c): The component schemes under PMKSY provide financial assistance in the form of 
grants-in-aid/subsidy for creation of modern food processing and preservation infrastructure. 
The scheme is aimed at creating modern food processing infrastructure and value addition 
facilities, strengthening the food processing sector, reducing post-harvest losses, enhancing the 
processing and preservation of agricultural produce, generating employment, and providing 
better remuneration to farmers. 

As on 30.06.2026, 1256 projects are operational under PMKSY, generating 9.16 lakh 
employment opportunities and creating 294.21 LMT per annum of processing and preservation 
capacity. The infrastructure created under the scheme has strengthened the food processing 
ecosystem, promoted value addition, improved supply chain efficiency, reduced post-harvest 
losses through the capacities created, and contributed to the growth of the food processing 
sector and exports of processed food products. 
 
(d) & (e):  MoFPI extends financial assistance under PMKSY for setting up or expansion of 
eligible projects. PMKSY is demand-driven in nature and funds are not 
allocated/sanctioned/released state-wise under any of the component schemes of PMKSY. 
Applications are invited through Expressions of Interest (EoIs) from all over the country, 
including Kosi-Seemanchal region of Bihar and Telangana. The proposals received are 
scrutinized for eligibility and evaluated as per the applicable scheme guidelines. Financial 
assistance is provided to eligible projects approved on merit, subject to availability of funds. 
Under PMKSY, no proposal from the Government of Telangana is pending for approval in the 
Ministry.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1968 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
INSTANCES OF UNRULY AND OBJECTIONABLE BEHAVIOUR OF 
AIR PASSENGERS  
1968.    SHRI ANIL YESHWANT DESAI                 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether instances of unruly and objectionable behaviour by air passengers including 
breaking of aircraft windows and misbehaviour with staff and other passengers have been 
reported posing a threat to the safety of passengers and aircraft; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the action taken against such unruly passengers in 
each such case; and 
 
(c) whether any punishment other than a travel ban has been awarded in this regard, if so, the 
details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a) to (c): As per Cabin Safety Circular 01 of 2025 issued by Directorate General of Civil 
Aviation (DGCA), any incident of p assenger misconduct/passenger rage/ unruly behaviour 
onboard, is to be immediately reported by airlines within 12 hours via email, and detailed 
written information is to be submitted to DGCA within 24 hours of the landing of the 
aircraft.; 
; 
In order to ensure safety of the aircraft/persons/property on board/good order & discipline on 
board and to handle the unlawful/disruptive behaviour on -board the aircraft, DGCA has 
issued CAR, Section n 3 - Air Transport, Series M, and Part VI titled "Handling of unruly / 
disruptive passengers".; 
; 
As per the said CAR, unruly passengers are generally categorised into three levels based on 
the severity of their misconduct onboard an aircraft. Based on the recommendation of the 
Internal Committee, formed in accordance with the CAR, these unruly passengers are banned 
from flying. The duration of flying ban imposed may vary with the severity level of 
misconduct.; 
; 
As on date, a total of 447 of passengers have been included in the 'No Fly List' since the 
issuance of the regulation on handling of unruly passengers in 2017.; 

; 
As per the procedure defined in the CAR, airlines are required to follow a prescribed 
procedure for holding passengers accountable before they are placed in the 'No Fly List' by 
the airline. Based on the in formation provided by the airlines, 'No Fly List' is maintained by 
DGCA.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PMEGP 
 
1969.   SHRI SUNIL BOSE: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of funds sanctioned, disbursed and utilised under the Prime Minister’s Employment 
Generation Programme (PMEGP) since its inception, State-wise particularly for the State of Karnataka; 
 
(b)  whether the union Government has evaluated the performance of the PMEGP in Tamil Nadu, a key 
industrial State and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c)  the details regarding the number of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs ) established 
and employment generated through this scheme in Karnataka; and 
 
(d)  whether any special measures have been taken to promote MSMEs in Chamarajanagar and Mysore 
districts and if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a):  Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) being a Central Sector Scheme, 
no State-wise allocation of budget is done. Funds are  disbursed based on the demand generated and loans 
sanctioned by the financial institutions  across States. State-wise details of Margin Money (MM) subsidy 
disbursed and utilised under PMEGP  since its inception i.e. FY 2008 -09 to FY 2025 -26 is given at 
Annexure. 
 
(b):  The Ministry conducted an evaluation of the PMEGP through a third party agency covering 28,200 
PMEGP beneficiary units and 2,800 non -beneficiary enterprises across all States/UTs, including 1,670 
PMEGP units of Tamil Nadu to assess the performance of the PMEGP units established during the period 
FY 2008-09 to FY 2023 -24. Most of the PMEGP units reported increase in average annual income and 
positive profitability across sectors over the years. 
 
(c):  Since its  inception of the scheme, 55,430 microenterprises have been assisted in the state of 
Karnataka generating estimated employment of 498,870 persons. 
 
(d): Initiatives undertaken by the Ministry of MSME under PMEGP to promote entrepreneurship and 
create job opportunities across the country including Chamaraj anagar and Mysore districts of Karnataka 
state are as follows: 

: 2 : 
 
 
 
i. Enhancement of maximum project cost from Rs. 25 lakh to Rs. 50 lakh for manufacturing sector and 
from Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 20 lakh for service sector. 
ii. Inclusion of applicants from Aspira tional districts and transgenders under Special Category eligible 
for higher subsidy. 
iii. Establishment of PMEGP Helpdesks at State Offices to provide real -time assistance and hand -
holding to potential beneficiaries. 
iv. A wide range of more than 1,000 Model of De tailed Project Reports prepared on various industries 
have been made available on the PMEGP portal. 
v. Disseminating Information, Education and Communication (IEC) material and video clips in 
regional languages for promotion in remote areas. 
vi. As per RBI Master  Directions on lending to MSMEs, no collateral security to be insisted by Banks 
for projects involving loan up to Rs. 20 lakh. Strict compliance of this provision has been 
reemphasized to all financing Banks. 
vii. Periodical review meetings by the Ministry with  Implementing Agencies i.e. KVIC, State offices of 
KVIC, State Khadi and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs), State District Industries Centres (DICs) 
and financial institutions. 
viii. Awareness and outreach programmes in all the States/UTs including backward and under- 
performing areas, Aspirational districts, NER etc. to identify potential beneficiaries and provide 
handholding support during the application process. 
ix. Financial literacy camps and customer awareness programmes conducted by Banks to educate 
prospective entrepreneurs about various initiatives of the Government, including PMEGP.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1970 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
  
STATUS OF EMRSs 
  
1970. SHRI ARUN BHARTI: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the current status of Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) across the country, including 
the number of schools sanctioned and those presently functional, particularly in Bihar; 
(b) the steps taken to expand the network of EMRSs, including the recent inaugurations and 
initiation of new school projects in various States; 
(c) the facilities and academic support systems being provided in EMRSs to improve educational 
outcomes and skill development among tribal students; 
(d) the measures adopted to ensure adequate staffing, quality infrastructure and timely 
operationalisation of sanctioned EMRSs; and 
(e) the manner in which the expansion of EMRSs aligns with the Government's objectives of 
inclusive education and empowerment of tribal communities? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI DURGADAS UIKEY) 
  
(a & b): As on date, 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) are approved across the 
country out of which 508 are functional. In Bihar, 03 EMRSs have been approved, of which 02 
EMRSs are functional. The inauguration of 43 new EMRSs during 2025-26 is an effort to expand 
the EMRS network in the country. 
  
(c): Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and sports facilities 
in EMRSs across the country which are well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, 
bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning 
resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, 
art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill 
development and vocational training programs on apparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & 
Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc. 
  
(d): To address the issue of vacancies, 9111 teaching & non -teaching staff have already been 
recruited and examination has been conducted for another batch of 7267 teaching & non -teaching 

staff for EMRSs across the country. In addition, State Governments have also been advised to 
depute staff on deputation and contract basis to address the issue of vacancies so that academic 
activities are not hampered.  
In order to bridge the infrastructure gap in EMRSs, several measures have been taken such as 
Standardised designs ensuring modern academic facilities, hostels, staff quarters, and sports 
infrastructure; additional grants for upgradation of old schools; regular monitoring through third-
party inspections etc. 
  
Further, National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) continuously follows up with 
the State Governments and the execution agencies to fast-track construction of EMRSs and to 
make them functional at the earliest. Besides, State Governments have also been advised to make 
the EMRS functional in alternative buildings, wherever feasible. 
  
(e): The expansion of EMRSs aligns with the Government's objectives of inclusive education and 
empowerment of tribal communities in the following manner: 
 EMRSs provide access to quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in 
remote and tribal-dominated areas, thereby reducing educational disparities.  
 The scheme promotes equitable access to educational opportunities by providing free 
education along with boarding and lodging facilities.  
 EMRSs focus on the holistic development of tribal students through academic excellence, 
sports, skill development, and extracurricular activities.  
 The scheme enhances educational attainment, employability and leadership potential 
among tribal youth, contributing to their socio-economic empowerment.  
 The expansion of EMRSs supports the Government's commitment to inclusive and 
accessible education for tribal communities across the country.

NO. 1973  ADV PRIYA SAROJ: 
SHRI PUSHPENDRA SAROJ: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the cities identified as vulnerable to urban flooding 
due to inadequate storm -water drainage, State-wise, particularly 
district-wise for Uttar Pradesh; 
(b) the details of the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) where storm -water 
drainage master plans have been prepared or updated since 2021, 
State-wise, particularly district-wise for Uttar Pradesh; 
(c) the details of the Central technical assistance provided for 
climate-resilient urban infrastructure and flood mitigation, State-
wise, particularly district-wise for Uttar Pradesh; 
(d) the details of the cities where integrated drainage projects are 
under preparation or implementation, State- wise, particularly 
district-wise for Uttar Pradesh; and 
(e) the measures taken to strengthen urban flood resilience under 
Central programmes?   
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
(a) to (e): Management of urban flooding falls under the purview of 
the State Governments and the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ Urban 
Development Authorities, who are responsible for maintaining the 
drainage and sewerage system. Government of India supplements the 
efforts of the States through schematic interventions/ advisories. It 
provides financial and technical support to the States to strengthen 
Urban Planning ecosystem. The data regarding cities vulnerable to 
urban flooding due to inadequate stormwater drainage is not maintained 
centrally.

of GIS based Master Plan for AMRUT cities, which is also applicable for 
Class-II cities/ towns, which inter alia provides for mapping of utility 
layers including Storm Water Drainage by the ULBs. 
The Government of India implemented the Scheme for Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SSASCI) in the years 2022-
23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 of which Urban Planning Reforms was 
a part. The scheme aimed at leveraging urban planning as a key driver 
of development. This initiative was focused on several critical themes, 
including creation of sponge cities. As claimed by the States under

SSASCI 2025 -26, 21 cities in 13 States have prepared Storm Water 
Drainage Plan. The details of the cities, state-wise is given in Annexure. 
Uttar Pradesh has not claimed the reform.  
Under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 
and AMRUT 2.0, States/ ULBs are supported through projects for storm 
water drainage, which involved construction and improvement of drains/ 
storm water drains in order to reduce and eliminate flooding,  creating 
green spaces and parks  and water body rejuvenation projects . The 
States/ Union Territories are empowered to select, appraise, prioritise 
and implement the projects within the broad framework of Mission 
guidelines.  
Under AMRUT, 838 Storm Water Drainage projects worth ₹3022.39 crore 
have been taken up by the States/Union Territories (UTs). Further, the 
States/ UTs have taken up 2,522 green spaces and park projects worth 
₹1,604.13 crore under AMRUT which has resulted in development of 
5,400 acres of permeable green space area through these projects.  
Under AMRUT 2.0, projects for green spaces and parks and rejuvenation 
of water bodies have been taken up by the States/UTs. Proposals of the 
States/ UTs for 2,951 water body rejuvenation projects worth ₹6,003.34 
crore covering around 1.21 lakh acres of area and 1,649 green spaces 
and park projects worth ₹1,087.12 crore covering around 12,750 acre 
have been approved under AMRUT 2.0.  
Besides, under AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0 sewerage and septage

sewer network. Under AMRUT 2.0, the State/UTs have taken up 605

40,021 km of sewer network. 
The State -wise and ULB -wise details of projects under AMRUT and  
AMRUT 2.0, including projects in Uttar Pradesh is available on the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA 
REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1974 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
DISTRICT WATER ACCOUNTS AND WATER SECURITY REPORT 
†1974. Smt. SANDHYA RAY: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware that despite va rious schemes being 
implemented in the country for conservation of rive rs, ponds, groundwater and 
rainwater, there is no integrated and public scient ific account available of the 
actual status of water resources of each district and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to prepare an a nnual "District Water Account 
and Water Security Report" for each district and if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether the Government also proposes to link th is report with the district plan 
and financial allocation, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 
(a) to (c) ‘Water’ being a State subject, the aspec ts related to water resources 
including its conservation are studied, planned, fu nded and executed by the State 
Governments themselves as per their own resources a nd priorities. The Central 
Government supplements the measures and efforts bei ng taken up by the State 
Governments. 
The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) undertakes re gular activities related 
to the exploration, monitoring, assessment and mana gement of groundwater 
resources across the country. Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country are 

2 
 
assessed annually since 2022 jointly by CGWB and th e respective State 
Governments/UT Administrations. The assessment prov ides scientific estimation of 
Annual Ground Water Recharge, Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource, Annual 
Ground Water Extraction and Stage of Ground Water E xtraction at the assessment-
unit level (Block/Mandal/Taluka/Tehsil/District, as  applicable). The results of the 
assessment are made available in the public domain through CGWB's online portal. 
As per the Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessmen t, 2025, the Total 
Annual Ground Water Recharge of the country is 448. 52 Billion Cubic Meter (BCM) 
and the Annual Extractable Ground Water Resource is  407.75 BCM. The Stage of 
Ground Water Extraction, which is a measure of Annual Ground Water Extraction for 
all uses (irrigation, industrial and domestic uses)  over Annual Extractable Ground 
Water Resource, is 60.63% for the country as a whole. 
Further, out of the total 6,762 assessment units in the country, 4,946 (73.14%) 
are categorized as ‘Safe’, 758 (11.21%) as ‘Semi-cr itical’, 201 (2.97%) as ‘Critical’, 
730 (10.80%) as ‘Over-exploited’ and 127 (1.88%) as  ‘Saline’. The details of district 
wise resources can be accessed through CGWB’s onlin e portal: 
https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf#page=171. 
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) i mplements the Atal 
Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2.0, under which cities 
prepare City Water Balance Plans (CWBPs) and City W ater Action Plan (CWAP). 
These CWAPs are aggregated in the form of State Water Action Plans (SWAP). 
Further, Village-level feasibility maps have been s hared with districts to 
support technical planning and facilitate the effec tive implementation of water 
conservation and groundwater recharge interventions . In addition, 651 districts 
across the country have prepared District Water Con servation Plans to ensure 
sustainable water management in their respective districts.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1975 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
DEVELOPMENT OF GREENFIELD AIRPORT AT DHANBAD  
1975.    SHRI DULU MAHATO                  
        
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the non -allocation of land and lack of consent by the State 
Government of Jharkhand is the main obstacle in the establishment of a 
greenfield airport and commencement of flight operations in Dhanbad; 
(b) whether i t is true that the construction of an airport would generate large -
scale employment opportunities, economic prosperity and revenue in the region 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of the correspondence made by the Union Government with the 
State Government of Jharkhand so far to resolve the impasse and facilitate the 
project; 
(d) whether the Union Government is considering an alternative model for 
developing an airport on unused land of any Central Public Sector Undertaking 
such as Coal India o r BCCL without depending on the said State Government 
and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the concrete steps proposed to be taken by the Union Government to provide 
air connectivity to Dhanbad and resolve the impasse? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): As per Greenfield Airports (GFA) Policy, 2008, any airport developer 
including the State Government desirous of developing a Greenfield airport are 
required to identify a suitable site and ge t the Pre -feasibility Study conducted 
and submit a proposal to the Central Government for 'Site Clearance' followed  
by an 'In-Principle' approval. 
 
As of now, no proposal seeking Site Clearance under GFA Policy has been 
received for construction of a Greenfield Airport in Dhanbad. 
 
As per the GFA Policy, the responsibility for implementation of the Greenfield 
airport projects including land acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement, 
funding, obtaining mandatory clearances etc. lies with the airport deve loper 
concerned or the State Government, as the case may be.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1976 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
EXPANSION OF KOLHAPUR AIRPORT  
1976.    SHRI SHAHU SHAHAJI CHHATRAPATI        
    
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the current operational status of Kolhapur Airport including passenger 
footfall, runway capacity and terminal infrastructure; 
(b) whether any proposal to expand the said airport is under consideration of the 
Government and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to sanction new routes connecting 
Kolhapur to cities beyond Mumbai, Pune and Goa including Hyderabad, Delhi 
and Bengaluru under the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) -UDAN and if 
so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the timeline fixed for upgrading Kolhapur Airport’s infrastructure to 
accommodate larger aircraft and increased flight frequency to meet growing 
passenger and cargo demand? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) & (b): Kolhapur Airport is an operational airport. The runway can cater to 
Code 3C (ATR-72) type aircraft operations. The terminal building has a built-up 
area of 3,900 sq. m and can cater to 500 peak -hour passengers and 0.5 million 
passengers per annum. Kolhapur Airport has handled 1.60, 1.59 and 1.72 Lakh 
passengers during 2023 -24, 2024-25 and 2025 -26 respectively. Expansion and 
development of airports is carried out based on passenger demand, operational 
requirements and airline demand.  Such development works are carried out in 
phases, subject to availability of land, financial viability and operational 
considerations. 
 
(c) : At present, Kolhapur Airport has scheduled connectivity to Bengaluru, 
Hyderabad, Navi Mumbai and Mumbai. Under t he modified UDAN Scheme, 
Kolhapur is categorized as a Served Airport. Accordingly, routes connecting 
Kolhapur are not eligible for bidding under the forthcoming bidding rounds. 

 
(d): Upgradation of airport infrastructure depends upon various factors, 
including traffic demand, operational requirements, availability of statutory and 
mandatory clearances, financial viability and other project -specific 
requirements.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1977 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
PERFORMANCE OF THE PRODUCTION LINKED INCENTIVE SCHEME 
  
1977. SHRI ASHISH DUBEY: 
SHRI YADUVEER WADIYAR: 
SHRI VIVEK THAKUR: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the current status and performance of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for 
the Food Processing Industries, especially in aspirational districts; 
(b) the extent of investment attracted, production achieved and employment generated/job 
created under the PLI scheme; 
(c) the current status of the development and operationalisation of Mega Food Parks along 
with their contribution to the growth of the organized food processing sector; and 
(d) the steps taken to boost the export of Indian food products, enhance their branding and 
adopt new technologies in the industry? 
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI CHIRAG PASWAN) 
 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Food Processing Industries is implementing the Production Linked 
Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) with an approved outlay of ₹10,900 
crore for the period from FY 2021-22 to FY 2026-27. The Scheme provides performance-
linked incentives on achievement of eligible incremental sales and aims to promote domestic 
processing and value addition, support creation of global food manufacturing champions, 
promote Indian food brands in overseas markets and generate employment opportunities. A 
total of 163 applications from 127 companies, including 69 Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs) are presently covered under the Scheme. The approved projects are 
spread across 212 locations in 22 States. Incentives amounting to ₹3,271.44 crore have been 
disbursed up to June 2026. The Scheme has contributed to expansion of food processing 
capacity, growth in sales and exports, mobilisation of investment and generation of 
employment. The investments undertaken under the Scheme have resulted in creation of food 
processing capacity of 34 lakh metric ton per annum. 
Approved applicants under PLISFPI have invested ₹9,207 crore against committed 
investment of ₹7,722 crore and generated approximately 3.35 lakh direct and indirect 
employment opportunities against the target of 2.50 lakh. Sales of PLI-supported products 
increased from ₹58,758 crore in FY 2019-20 to ₹1,08,854 crore in FY 2025-26.  

Details of the units approved under the PLISFPI in aspirational districts are provided in 
the Annexure. 
(c): The Ministry implemented the Mega Food Park Scheme, a component scheme under the 
umbrella scheme Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana since 2008. The Scheme followed a 
cluster-based hub-and-spoke approach for creation of primary processing, storage, common 
processing and enabling infrastructure. The Mega Food Park Scheme has been discontinued 
with effect from 01.04.2021. A total of 41 Mega Food Parks in 25 States have been approved 
under the Scheme, of which 25 are operational. These projects are expected to create 
preservation capacity of 28.57 Lakh Metric Ton Per Annum (LMTPA) and processing capacity 
of 15.41 LMTPA, benefitting approximately 86,881 farmers and generating 1,02,440 direct 
and indirect employment opportunities. 
(d):  Under PLISFPI, the Government promotes exports and branding of Indian food products 
abroad through the Branding and Marketing component. Approved applicants are provided 
financial incentives at the rate of 50 per cent of eligible expenditure incurred on Branding and 
Marketing Abroad, subject to a maximum of 3 per cent of sales of food products or ₹50 crore 
per year, whichever is less. The PLISFPI also promotes domestic processing and value addition 
through performance-linked incentives on eligible incremental sales. The investments 
undertaken by approved applicants have facilitated expansion of processing capacity and 
adoption of modern processing, packaging and manufacturing technologies. A separate 
category has also been provided under the Scheme for Small & Medium Enterprises (SMEs) 
engaged in innovative and organic food products. 
The Ministry is also implementing Prime Minister Formalisation of Micro Food 
Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme. PMFME Scheme is a demand driven scheme aimed 
at providing financial, technical and business support for setting up or upgradation of micro 
food processing enterprises through capacity building, credit support, technology upgradation 
and market linkages. The Scheme supports establishment of new enterprises and upgradation 
of existing enterprises through 35% credit-linked capital subsidy (maximum ₹10 lakh per unit), 
establishment of Common Infrastructure and Common Incubation Centers (CICs) with modern 
processing, testing, packaging and storage infrastructure, and provides Branding & Marketing 
support of up to 50% of the eligible project cost for development of common brands, 
packaging, labelling and quality standardization. To promote adoption of modern technologies 
and improve export readiness, the Scheme provides Entrepreneurship Development 
Programmes (EDP), product-specific training and technical support through National Institute 
of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM) and State Level Technical 
Institutions.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1978 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
REGULATORY FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE AVIATION 
FUEL  
1978.    SHRI TANUJ PUNIA                         
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has amended the Aviation Turbine Fuel Rules to legalise the 
blending of ethanol and synthetic hydrocarbons in aircraft fuel and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of the safety and t esting standards being adopted to address technical concerns 
regarding engine blockage or freezing of ethanol -blended fuel due to low temperatures while 
flying at high altitudes; and 
 
(c) the current production capacity of ethanol -based ‘Alcohol-to-Jet’ plants in the country to 
meet the target of one per cent Sustainable Aviation Fuel for international flights by 2027? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a): The Government has notified an amendment to the Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) 
(Regulation of Marketing) Order, 2001 (ATF Control Order) vide notification dated 17 April 
2026 to bring ATF blended with Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) under the ambit of the ATF 
Control Order. 
 
(b) & (c): The safety and techn ical requirements for SAF are governed by internationally 
accepted standards. ASTM D4054 prescribes the qualification and certification process for 
new aviation fuels, including laboratory, engine and flight testing to establish that they meet 
the performa nce and safety standards of conventional aviation turbine fuel. ASTM D7566 
specifies the approved production pathways and blending requirements for SAF, while 
ASTM D1655 lays down the specifications for the final blended aviation turbine fuel. 
Accordingly, only SAF produced through ASTM -approved pathways and blended within the 
prescribed limits is permitted for use in aircraft.; 
 
The Government has approved indicative blending targets of 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028, and 
5% by 2030 for SAF in conventional Aviatio n Turbine Fuel for international operations. 
Public sector Oil Marketing Companies are actively engaged in achieving the stated blending 
targets.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1980 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
INQUIRY REPORT ON CRASH OF AIR INDIA FLIGHT 
1980.    SHRI VIJAY KUMAR HANSDAK                 
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
a) the current status and the timeline fixed for the completion and publication of the final 
inquiry report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau into the crash of Air India (AI) 
171 at Ahmedabad on June 12, 2025; 
 
(b) whether the Government has taken note of conflicting theories regarding the “fuel switch 
cut-off” mechanism and if so, the details thereof including technical findings that have 
emerged from the analysis of the aircraft’s Black Boxes; 
 
(c) whether the en gines and main computer network components were sent abroad for 
technical evaluation and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether any critical safety data is currently being withheld by foreign manufacturers or 
entities and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) the response of the Government to safety concerns raised by aviation bodies and 
independent safety experts regarding potential electrical or systemic failures in early -model 
Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner aircraft? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of  CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Murlidhar 
Mohol) 
(a): A preliminary investigation report has been published on 12 Jul 2025, and the interim 
statement was published on 12 June 2026 by Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), 
same are available on AAIB website.; 
; 
 The investigation is under progress. All probable causes leading to the accident are being 
investigated. The final investigation report will be published after completion of the 
investigation.; 
; 
(b) to (d): The investigation is looking into all t he aspects to identify the root cause and 
contributing factors leading to the accident.; 
; 
(e): Aircraft safety issues are addressed by the State of Design authorities alongside the 
Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) via Airworthiness Directives (ADs) and Service 

Bulletins (SBs). Operators must comply with all mandatory requirements under Civil 
Aviation Requirements (CARs). The Directorate General of Civil Aviation enforces 
compliance across Indian -registered aircraft through Airworthiness Review Certif icate 
inspections, regular surveillance, and continuous oversight.; 
; 
In respect of early -model B787 issues, mandatory actions were executed -notably Federal

enhanced lit hium-ion battery containment and ventilation. Subsequent ADs and SBs for 
electrical, fuel, software, wiring, engine, and structural systems have been continually 
implemented and monitored to ensure fleet safety.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA 
REJUVENATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1982 
ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
IMPLEMENTATION OF ABY IN TAMIL NADU 
1982. Shri MALAIYARASAN D: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of implementation of Atal Bh ujal Yojana (ABY) in Tamil 
Nadu including the number of districts, blocks and Gram Panchayats covered 
thereunder, particularly in Kallakurichi Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(b) the details of the funds allocated, released an d utilised under ABY for 
groundwater management and conservation activities in Tamil Nadu during the 
last five years; 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of ABY on groundwater 
levels, water conservation practices and community participation in the 
identified areas and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has identified over-expl oited and critical 
groundwater blocks in Tamil Nadu requiring urgent i ntervention and if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(e) the steps being taken by the Government to prom ote groundwater 
recharge, rainwater harvesting, efficient water use  and sustainable 
groundwater management in water-stressed regions of Tamil Nadu? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI  
(SHRI RAJ BHUSHAN CHOUDHARY) 

2 
 
(a) & (b)   Atal Bhujal Yojana was a pilot scheme w ith a fixed duration and 
outlay, implemented across 8,203 water-stressed Gra m Panchayats in seven 
States, namely, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Mahara shtra, Karnataka, Madhya 
Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. The Scheme has now ended  after successfully 
demonstrating the efficacy of community-led partici patory groundwater 
management and providing a replicable model which c an be taken up for 
implementation by other States also. The scheme was  not implemented in the 
State of Tamil Nadu during the pilot stage. 
  
(c)   An Overall Impact Assessment Study of Atal Bhujal Y ojana has been 
conducted by the Quality Council of India (QCI). Ba sed on detailed field 
surveys conducted in the Scheme implementation area s and interactions with 
local communities, the study has recognized importa nt changes brought about 
by the scheme, like enhanced community awareness on  groundwater issues 
through capacity-building and IEC activities, women 's participation in 
leadership and decision-making in groundwater manag ement, social inclusivity 
and an overall knowledge enhancement and willingnes s of the community to 
partake in groundwater conservation and water manag ement. A copy of this 
Report is available on the website of Department of  Water Resources, River 
Development and Ganga Rejuvenation at the following web-link: 
https://www.jalshakti-
dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/07/597fd8727a8d10641bd33d7d22ce0459.pdf  
  
(d)   Dynamic Ground Water Resources of the country, incl uding those of the 
State of Tamil Nadu, are being assessed annually fr om 2022 jointly by the 
Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) and the respectiv e State Governments. 
The assessment estimates Annual Groundwater Recharg e, Annual Extractable 
Groundwater Resource, Annual Groundwater Extraction , and the Stage of 
Groundwater Extraction, and categorizes assessment units as Safe, Semi-
Critical, Critical, Over-exploited (OCS), and Salin e. The assessment is utilized 

3 
 
to identify groundwater-stressed areas and provides  a scientific basis for 
planning sustainable groundwater management measure s, including artificial 
recharge, rainwater harvesting, aquifer management and regulation of 
groundwater extraction. The block-wise Ground Water  Resources and OCS 
categorization for the State of Tamil Nadu (2025) a re available on the website 
of the Department of Water Resources, River Develop ment and Ganga 
Rejuvenation at the following web-link: 
https://www.jalshakti-
dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/07/5f94f781426143f043e1a63f58f95487.pdf  
  
(e) Water being a State subject, the responsibility of addressing the 
groundwater related issues lies primarily with the concerned State 
Governments. However, the Central Government facili tates the efforts of the 
State Governments by way of technical and financial  assistance through its 
various schemes and projects. The important steps t aken by the Government 
for groundwater conservation and replenishment thro ugh rainwater harvesting, 
artificial recharge, and regulation of groundwater extraction in the country, 
including in Tamil Nadu, are given below:- 
i. Under Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA), an annual mission m ode programme for 
taking up water harvesting and artificial recharge activities, more than 
2.0 crore water conservation and artificial recharg e works have been 
taken up through convergence in the country so far,  with more than 
18.55 lakh works in Tamil Nadu. This has played a k ey role in enhancing 
the sustainability of ground water resources, parti cularly in water-
stressed districts. 
ii. Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative has bee n launched by the 
Hon’ble Prime Minister in 2024 with a vision to mak e rainwater 
harvesting a mass movement in the country. By promo ting community 
ownership and responsibility, the initiative seeks to develop cost-

4 
 
effective, local solutions tailored to specific wat er challenges across 
districts. By 31st May 2026, more than 1.55 crore a rtificial groundwater 
recharge and storage works have been reported to be  constructed 
across the country under this initiative, with arou nd 3.15 lakh such 
structures in Tamil Nadu.  
iii. On 01 June 2026 JSJB-Catch the Rain (CTR) has been launched nation-
wide with a special focus on accelerating groundwater recharge in over-
exploited and critical districts through low-cost, hyper-local 
interventions. JSJB: CTR is driven by Jan Bhagidari , mobilizing 
Panchayati Raj Institutions, Urban Local Bodies, wo men's groups, 
youth, educational institutions, civil society orga nizations, and local 
communities to actively participate in water conservation efforts. 
iv. Mission Amrit Sarovar was launched in 2022 by the G overnment of 
India, which aimed at developing and rejuvenating 7 5 water bodies in 
each district of the country, including Tamil Nadu.  As an outcome, 
nearly 69,000 Amrit Sarovars have been constructed/  rejuvenated in the 
country, with 2,484 in Tamil Nadu. 
v. From 01.04.2025 till 30.06.2026, 15,08,921 water re lated works have 
been completed in the Country, including 1,09,479 w orks in the State of 
Tamil Nadu, under MGNREGS. The Viksit Bharat-Guaran tee for Rozgar 
and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act 2025 has been imp lemented with 
effect from 01.07.2026. Water security is one of th e key features of the 
VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. 
vi. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has circu lated the Model 
Building Bye-laws, 2016, which recommend the adopti on of rainwater 
harvesting systems in all buildings having a plot s ize of 100 sq. metres 
or more. So far, 35 States / UTs, including Tamil N adu, have 
incorporated these provisions in their respective building bye-laws. 

5 
 
vii. The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was launched 
during the year 2015-16, with the aim to enhance ph ysical access of 
water on farm and expand cultivable area under assu red irrigation, 
improve on-farm water use efficiency, introduce sus tainable water 
conservation practices, etc.  Under the Accelerated  Irrigation Benefits 
Programme and Command Area Development & Water Mana gement 
components of PMKSY., 30.66 lakh hectare irrigation  potential has been 
created, with pari passu development of 23.42 lakh hectare command 
area has been achieved. Under the PMKSY-Har Khet Ko  Pani (HKPP), 
Repair, Renovation & Restoration (RRR) of water bod ies, works of 645 
water bodies/tanks in various districts of Tamil Na du have been taken 
up, out of which restoration works of 571 water bod ies/tanks have been 
completed up to March, 2026. 
viii. CGWB has completed the National Aquifer Mapping (NA QUIM) 1.0 
covering the country’s mappable area of about 25 la kh sq. kms, 
including  entire mappable area of about 1,05,742 s q. km spread across 
all 38 districts of Tamil Nadu. Aquifer maps and gr oundwater 
management plans, including both demand-side and su pply-side 
interventions for sustainable groundwater managemen t, have been 
prepared and shared with the concerned State agenci es for 
implementation.  Under NAQUIM 2.0 state-of-the-art technologies are 
harnessed for generating highly detailed scientific  data, for making 
informed decisions about sustainable groundwater management. 
ix. CGWB has prepared the Master Plan for Artificial Re charge to 
Groundwater-2020 for the entire country and shared with States / UTs. 
The Master Plan serves as a technical guide for pla nning and 
implementation of rainwater harvesting and artifici al recharge 
structures in districts based on local hydrogeological conditions.  

6 
 
x. CGWB conducts various outreach and awareness progra mmes, 
including Public Interaction Programmes, Mass Aware ness 
Programmes, Tier-II and Tier-III trainings on local  groundwater issues, 
to create awareness regarding rainwater harvesting techniques and the 
conservation of water harvesting structures. 
xi. The Ministry of Jal Shakti has notified Guidelines dated 24.09.2020 and 
subsequent amendments dated 29.03.2023 for the regu lation of 
groundwater extraction by industries, infrastructur e and mining 
projects. States/UTs are being encouraged to adopt or align their 
existing regulations accordingly. CGWA also issues directions to 
States/UTs for adopting rooftop rainwater harvestin g in all Critical and 
Over-Exploited assessment units across the country and in Government 
buildings under their jurisdiction. 
xii. The Ministry of Jal Shakti has circulated a Model B ill to all States/UTs 
to facilitate the enactment of groundwater legislat ion for regulating 
groundwater development, including provision for ra inwater harvesting. 
So far, 21 States/UTs have adopted and implemented such legislation. 
In Tamil Nadu, groundwater regulation is presently being carried out 
through Government Orders. 
xiii. The Directorate of Town Panchayats, Govt. of Tamil Nadu is actively 
engaged in the construction of rooftop rainwater ha rvesting structures 
on all government, commercial and residential build ings. Further, under 
various state government projects like Tamil Nadu I rrigated Agriculture 
Modernization Project (TNIAMP), Mission on Sustaina ble Dryland 
Agriculture (MSDA), Chief Minister’s Dryland Develo pment Mission 
(CMDDM) etc. large-scale construction of farm ponds  and check dams 
has been taken up across the state.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI 
DEPARTMENT OF DRINKING WATER & SANITATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1983 
ANSWERED ON 30/07/2026 
 
WATER QUALITY MANAGEMENT UNDER JAL JEEVAN MISSION 
 
1983. SHRI RAO RAJENDRA SINGH: 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) the measures taken to ensure the quality of tap water supplied to households under the Jal  
Jeevan Mission (JJM);  
(b) the details of water quality testing and monitoring mechanisms established under the  
Mission;  
(c) the details of water treatment facilities created or upgraded to ensure safe drinking water  
supply under the Mission; and  
(d) the steps taken to address contamination of drinking water sources and ensure compliance  
with prescribed water quality standards under the Mission? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI V. SOMANNA) 
 
(a) to (d) Drinking Water being a state subject, the responsibility of planning, approval,  
implementation, operation, and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including those 
under the JJM, lies with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supplements the  
efforts of the States/ UTs by providing financial, policy guidance and technical assistance. Jal  
Jeevan Mission is under implementation since August, 2019, to make  provision of tap water  
supply to every rural household. Under JJM, as per existing guidelines, Bureau of Indian  
Standards’ BIS:10500 standards are adopted as benchmark for quality of water being supplied 
through the piped water supply schemes. 
Under JJM, while planning water supply schemes to provide tap water supply to households,  
priority is given to habitations affected by chemical contaminants. States/ UTs have been  
advised to plan and implement piped water supply schemes based on alternative safe wate r 
sources for the villages with water quality issues. Further, States/ UTs have been advised to  
install community water purification plants (CWPPs) especially in Arsenic and Fluoride  

Page 2 of 2 
 
affected habitations to provide potable water to every household to meet their drinking and  
cooking requirements (to the tune of 8 -10 litres per capita per day) till the commissioning of  
piped water supply schemes compliant to JJM standards.  
As per the Operational Guidelines, States/ UTs can utilize JJM funds for Water Quality  
Monitoring & Surveillance (WQM&S) activities, inter -alia, which includes setting up and  
strengthening of water quality testing laboratories, procurement of equipment, instruments,  
chemicals, glassware, consumables, hiring of skilled manpower, surveillance  by community 
using field test kits (FTKs), awareness generation, educational programmes on water quality,  
accreditation/recognition of laboratories, etc.  
Under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), to enable States/ UTs to test water samples for water  
quality, and for sample collection, reporting, monitoring and surveillance of drinking water, an 
online JJM – Water Quality Management Information System (JJM-WQMIS) portal has been 
developed. The State–wise details of water quality testing reported through WQMIS are made 
available in public domain and can be accessed at:  
https://ejalshakti.gov.in/WQMIS/Main/report.  
In consultation with various stakeholders 'Concise Handbook for Monitoring Water Quality of 
Piped Drinking Water Supply to Rural Households’ was released in December 2024 for  
guidance to States/ UT’s. This handbook recommended for a comprehensive testing of drinking 
water samples at various testing points such as source, treatment plant, storage and distribution 
points, and remedial action wherever necessary, to ensure that the water supplied to households 
is of prescribed quality (BIS:10500).  
Another Handbook on Drinking Water Treatment Technologies was released in March 2023  
to disseminate info rmation regarding technologies available amongst all stakeholders to  
understand and implement the new technologies that address local issues and challenges faced 
in water -quality affected villages. The States may take up appropriate numbers of water  
treatment system of one or a combination of technologies depending upon techno -economic 
feasibility.  
States/ UTs have been advised to plan and implement piped water supply schemes based on  
alternative safe water sources/ bulk water transfer for the villages wit h water quality  issues. 
Moreover, any water supply scheme undertaken under JJM is approved only after th e 
recommendation of a Source Finding Committee of the respective State Government, to the  
effect that the identified water source through which the scheme is planned, has sufficient yield 
for sustaining water supply as per required norm, for the scheme design period.

1987. SHRI CHAVAN RAVINDRA VASANTRAO 
 SHRI SELVAGANAPATHI T.M: 
 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğी 
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of reports, including findings attributed to the Automotive 
Research Association of India (ARAI), indicating that the use of E20 petrol may adversely 
affect the engines, fuel systems, rubber components and certain plastic parts, including 
gaskets of vehicles designed for or compliant with E10 fuel;  
(b)  if so, the details thereof along with the Government's assessment of the number and 
categories of vehicles that are likely to be affected;  
(c)  whether it is also a fact that the use of E20 petrol may accelerate the deterioration of certain 
fuel system components in E10-compliant vehicles; and 
(d)  whether the Government has examined the implications of the introduction of E20 petrol on 
matters relating to compensation warranty, insurance coverage etc. and, if so, the details 
thereof? 
ANSWER 
पेĚोͧलयम और Ĥाकृ Ǔतक गैस मंğालय मɅ राÏय मंğी 
(Įी सुरेश गोपी) 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS  
 (SHRI SURESH GOPI) 
(a) to (d) :  The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a 
phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile 
manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India 
(ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) 
and other technical institutions. 
The rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with 
automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs). 
Extensive laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, IOCL, IIP and automobile 
manufacturers covering parameters such as engine durability, drivability, startability, corrosion 
resistance, material compatibility, emissions and fuel efficiency have confirmed that E20 is safe for 
use under prescribed standards. 
These studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in 
performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. These extensive laboratory studies, field 

validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact 
on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel. 
The Government's assessment is based not only on laboratory research but also on large-scale 
experience after nationwide implementation. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting 
retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles). 
This is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three-and-
a-half years and E19-E20 fuel for over two-and-a-half years. More than 20 crore two-wheelers and 
over 3 crore petrol cars have been operating on these blends without any verified evidence of 
widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending. Manufacturer 
service data confirm that there is no abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 
fuel. Manufacturers continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel, providing 
further confidence in its safety and reliability. 
A leading OEM serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including approximately 1.5 crore 
vehicles that were not originally certified as E20-compatible, and reported no E20-linked corrosion, 
abnormal wear or reduction in component life. A leading 2-wheeler company has reported similar 
field experience. One OEM recently stated that data from 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles tracked 
over an extended period showed no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion. ARAI reaffirmed that 
vehicles undergo rigorous international-standard validation before reaching consumers. 
Automobile manufacturers, component suppliers, SIAM, ARAI, testing agencies and Oil Marketing 
Companies were associated with every stage of the scientific evaluation and phased rollout of E20. 
E20 was introduced only after successful validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, 
material compatibility and emissions performance. These studies did not reveal any significant 
adverse impact on performance, durability or material compatibility in legacy vehicles under the 
prescribed operating conditions. Had automobile manufacturers not been fully satisfied with the 
results, they would neither have validated E20 fuel for older vehicles nor honoured warranty 
obligations. 
According to SIAM and ARAI, E20 improves acceleration and ride quality while reducing carbon 
emissions. Ethanol's higher-octane number supports modern high-compression engines and its 
higher heat of vaporisation improves combustion efficiency.

(a) to (c) The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been

consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, 
Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), Automotive Research Association of 

India (ARAI), Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), 
Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP) and other technical institutions.  
In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme commenced 
with a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and although blending 
remained around 1.53% in 2013 -14, it has since been increased 
progressively in a calibrat ed manner after creating the necessary 
production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework. 
E15+ blended petrol has been in widespread use for over three -and-a-

continue to honour warranty obligations for vehicles using E20 fuel,

A study for evaluation of effect of E20 on BS -III, BS-IV and BS -VI E10

and vehicle tests on road have not shown any failures due to E20.

approximately 30% lower c arbon emissions compared to E10 fuel.

33/11 KV e-House substation of 25 MVA to provide the power to 11 KV industrial 
& commercial consumers in the region of Hazaribagh.  
 
 Further, DVC is planning the following works in their command area (in 
the region of Hazaribagh): 
 
(i) Capacity Augmentation at DVC, Hazaribagh by replacing one no. 50 
MVA, 132/33KV transformer with 80MVA, 132/33KV transformer.  
 
(ii)  Re-conductoring & uprating of 132KV D/C Barhi - Hazaribagh line with 
HTLS conductor. 
 
Government of India (GoI) has taken several initiatives to strengthen the 
distribution sector which are as given below: 
 
(i)  Under, Revamped Dis tribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), launched in July 
2021, projects worth Rs.4,326 Crore (858 Rs. Cr. for smart metering works and 
3,468 Rs. Cr. for distribution infrastructure/loss -reduction works) have been 
sanctioned for the state of Jharkhand. The sanction ed works are expected to 
be completed by the sunset date of the scheme i.e. 31.03.2028. The details in 
respect of Lok Sabha constituency of Hazaribagh, is placed at Annexure-II. 
 
(ii)  In addition to RDSS, other initiatives are as under: 
 
I. Additional Borrowing consent of 0.5% of Gross Sate Domestic Product 
(GSDP) to State Governments, which is conditional on them undertaking 
specific reforms in the power sector.  
 
II. Additional Prudential Norms for sanctioning of loans to State owned 
power utilities contingent o n the performance of power distribution 
utilities against prescribed conditions. 
 
III. Rules for implementation of Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment 
(FPPCA) and cost reflective tariff so as to ensure that all prudent cost for 
supply of electricity is passed through. 
 
IV. Rules and Standard Operating Procedure issued for proper subsidy 
accounting and their timely payment. 
 
(c) :  There are no specific proposals  with this Ministry for transmission and 
distribution infrastructure works to be undertaken in the Hazaribagh Lok Sabha 
constituency.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1995 
ANSWERED ON 30TH JULY, 2026 
  
DEVELOPMENT OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS IN AMRITSAR 
  
1995. SHRI GURJEET SINGH AUJLA: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether the Government is aware that the Amritsar border belt despite 
being one of India's important international tourism and border regions, 
continues to lag behind in highway infrastructure and development compared 
to several other States and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government is aware that Amritsar receives a large number 
of tourists, pilgrims and business travellers every day but lacks world -class 
road connectivity and modern highway infrastructure commensurate with its 
national importance and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(c) whether several ongoing National Highway projects in the Amritsar region 
are progressing at a slow pace, resulting in delays in their comp letion and if 
so, the details thereof; 
  
(d) the reasons for such delays in execution of National Highway projects in 
the region; and 
  
(e) whether the Government proposes to accord priority to the expeditious 
completion of pending projects and development  of state-of-the-art highway 
infrastructure in the Amritsar border belt and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  

(a) and (b) The Government in Ministry of Road Transport &  Highways is 
responsible for the development and maintenance of National Highways in 
the country. Amritsar is well -connected through an extensive National 
Highway network providing connectivity to major cities, neighbouring States 
and the international border such as Jalandhar/Chandigarh/Delhi connectivity 
through the Jalandhar -Amritsar Highway (NH -3); Bathinda/Rajasthan 
connectivity through the Amritsar -Tarn Taran -Harike Highway (NH -54); 
Jammu & Kashmir connectivity through the Amritsar -Pathankot Highway 
(NH-54); and Himachal Pradesh connectivity through the Amritsar -Una 
Highway (NH -503A). The International Border is connected through the 
National Highway network linking Amritsar with Attari -Wagah (NH -3), 
providing direct access to this important border and tourist destination. 
Keeping in view Amritsar's national importance in terms of heritage, 
culture and socio -religious significance, the Government has taken up 
several measures to enhance the travel experience and improve convenience 
for tourists travelli ng to Amritsar by road. The important National Highway 
development projects taken up in and around Amritsar include the Delhi -
Amritsar-Katra Expressway and its spur to Amritsar, Amritsar Bypass (to 
facilitate movement of visitors to the Attari -Wagah Border), Amritsar-Ramdas 
corridor (to facilitate tourists visiting Kartarpur Sahib), Amritsar-Una Corridor 
(connecting Amritsar to Anandpur Sahib) and Beas -Batala-Dera Baba Nanak 
corridor (connecting Beas to the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor). 
  
(c), (d) and (e) Some  of the ongoing National Highway projects in the 
Amritsar region have faced delays, mainly on account of delay in acquistion 
of land, law and order issues, farmer's protests/agitations, demands for 
additional or elevated structures, non -reimbursement of po nd ash 
transportation cost by State Thermal Power Plants, delay in statutory 
clearances/permissions and force majeure events such as heavy rainfall and 
floods. All requisite actions are being taken up in consultation with State 
Government, District Administration and other stakeholders to resolve these 
issues. 
  
The Government accords high priority to these projects and the 
progress of these projects in the Amritsar region is being regularly reviewed 
and monitored at various levels in consultation with all the stakeholders, 
including through the Project Monitoring Group (PMG) Portal/PRAGATI portal. 
The Government is taking all necessary steps to expedite completion of 
these projects.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1996 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 30.07.2026 
 
AI-BASED LITERACY AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR MSMEs 
 
1996.   MS. PRANITI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE: 
 
Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has initiated or proposed any programmes to promote Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) -based literacy and digital capacity building among Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs) and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b)  the details of schemes or partnerships with industry, academic institutions, or technology 
platforms to provide AI training, tools and advisory support to MSMEs;  
 
(c)  whether any assessment has been conducted on the adoption of AI technologies by MSMEs 
and the challenges faced, including cost, skills gap and access to infrastructure and if so, the details 
thereof; and  
 
(d)  the steps taken or proposed to ensure inclusive access to AI -driven solutions for MSMEs, 
particularly in rural and semi-urban areas, to enhance productivity and competitiveness? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d):  The Government is taking several measures to promote  adoption of Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies among MSMEs. The Ministry of Electronics and 
Information Technology (MeitY) is implementing the IndiaAI Mission, approved on 7th March, 
2024 with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore. The Mission comprises seven pillars, namely, IndiaAI 
Compute Capacity, IndiaAI Innovation Centre, IndiaAI Datasets Platform, IndiaAI Application 
Development Initiative, IndiaAI Future  Skills, IndiaAI Startup Financing and Safe & Trusted AI, 
aimed at democratizing the benefits of AI across all strata of society, strengthening the AI innovation 
ecosystem and ensuring socially impactful, responsible and inclusive growth, including facilitating 
AI adoption across sectors. The Mission aims to democratize the benefits of AI across all strata of 
society including MSMEs to enhance their productivity and competitiveness. 
 
The Government periodically assesses the extent of digital adoption among MSMEs through 
evaluation studies in collaboration with industry and research institut ions. The Output -Outcome 
Monitoring Framework (OOMF) of NITI Aayog also serves as an institutional mechanism for 
evaluating outcomes of Government interventions. 
 
****

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. : 1997 
 ( TO BE ANSWERED ON THE  30th July 2026 )  
DEVELOPMENT OF DAGADARTHI AIRPORT  
1997.    SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY      
      
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) the timeline when the Dagadarthi Airport in Nellore district of Andhra 
Pradesh was sanctioned; 
(b) whether it is true that the Request for Proposals (RFPs) for design, build, 
finance, operate and transfer of the said airport was invi ted long back and if so, 
the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also true that the bids have been approved for the said purpose;  
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for the delay and the time by 
which the construction work of the airport is expected to commence; and 
(e) the time by which the First Phase of the project is expected to be completed 
and opened for public use? 
ANSWER 
Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION       
(Shri Murlidhar Mohol) 
(a) to (e): Government of India  (GoI) has granted 'In -Principle' approval to 
Government of Andhra Pradesh (GoAP) in 2016 for development of a 
Greenfield Airport at Dagadarthi (Nellore).   
 
Initially on 07.06.2016, tenders were invited by GoAP for development of the 
airport under Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode. The Concession 
Agreement signed in June, 2018 was later terminated in 2020 due to non -
conclusive financial closure by the selected bidder.  Further tender for selection 
of PPP Concessionaire was floated on 05.09.2025 followe d by second call on 
05.03.2026 and third call on 29.05.2026. No bids have been approved till date. 
 
As per Greenfield Airports Policy, the responsibility of implementation of 
airport projects rests with the airport developer concerned including the 
respective State Government (in case the State Government is the project 
proponent). The timeline for construction of an airport depends upon many 
factors, such as, land acquisition, availability of mandatory clea rances, financial 
closure, etc.

AIR COURIER FACILITY AT TIRUCHIRAPPALLI INTERNATIONAL 
AIRPORT  
1999.    SHRI DURAI VAIKO                      
    
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the Air Courier Facility at 
Tiruchirappalli International Airport is yet to become operational despite the 
necessary infrastructure being in place and if so, the deta ils thereof along with 
the reasons for delay in operationalising the said facility; 
(b) the present status of the proposal for commencing the Air Courier Facility at 
Tiruchirappalli International Airport; and 
(c) whether the Government proposes to expedite  the operationalisation of the 
facility at the said airport to promote exports, improve logistics and benefit 
MSMEs, traders and the public in the region and if so, the details thereof along 
with the timeline fixed in this regard?

(Shri Murlidhar Mohol)
